In particular, C$_{10}$H$_2$ exhibits much stronger plateau harmonics than C$_2$H$_2$, while the intermediate molecule C$_6$H$_2$ shows harmonic intensities between those of C$_2$H$_2$ and C$_{10}$H$_2$. Time-frequency analysis and charge-density evolution reveal that the enhanced HHG emission in longer chains originates from the enlarged electron acceleration distance and increased probability of multi-center recollision, especially near the terminal carbon atoms. These findings demonstrate that molecular-size engineering offers an effective strategy for controlling harmonic emission and optimizing attosecond light sources in extended molecular systems.

title: Encoded but Exposed: Language Embeddings can Reveal More Than They Should in Recommender Systems
abstract: Language embeddings are increasingly used in recommenders to represent item content, but their privacy risks remain poorly understood. We study whether item embeddings can reveal item identities when an adversary has access to auxiliary item text from external sources. We show that a simple cosine-similarity attack can recover item identities with high mean reciprocal rank across language models and candidate-set settings on two real-world datasets. Leakage is strongest when the adversary's partial information overlaps with the victim representation, but it also persists through semantic alignment between independently sourced descriptions. We further show that item leakage can propagate to user re-identification from sparse ratings. Finally, we evaluate obfuscated descriptions as a mitigation and find a clear leakage-utility tradeoff.

title: Realization Divergence in Multi-Provider Quantum Computing: A Pre-Registered Study of What Survives Measurement
abstract: Quantum programs pass through compilers, transpilers and vendor services before execution. However, the distance between what was written and what runs is rarely measured. We call this distance realization divergence: the observable difference in how an identical source circuit is realized and behaves across quantum software stacks. We report a hardware study across three vendors and four devices, combining pre-registered predictions with explicitly identified exploratory analyses and amendments. In a compilation experiment with assigned placement policies, embedding radius correlates with two-qubit overhead at Spearman 0.805, against 0.492 for circuit size. Under a fixed lowest-index policy, an eight-qubit Bernstein-Vazirani circuit exhibits greater execution divergence than a twelve-qubit circuit on IQM Emerald. The opposite ordering occurs on IQM Garnet. Both comparisons replicate across two repetitions with disjoint confidence intervals. These results support a placement-dependent explanation, without isolating individual hardware noise mechanisms. The same ordering inversion is absent on the all-to-all IonQ control. On Rigetti Cepheus, a follow-up using topology-aware native placement found no consistent advantage in correct-answer probability for either submission track, but did not establish equivalence between the tracks. Structural comparisons depend on metric weighting, placement and device generation. Provider interfaces also limit observability: Rigetti's supported-operation list remained unchanged across a device generation that replaced the native entangler. We classify silent interface failures in composed toolchains and identify checks at toolchain boundaries, connecting valid cross-provider comparisons with concrete software-quality practices.

title: Recovery of coefficients in a Schrödinger system with nonlinear coupling
abstract: We consider the inverse problem of recovering time-dependent coefficients in a system of Schrödinger equations with coupled nonlinear terms. We first address the well-posedness of the system for small boundary data and trivial initial data. Then, we show that the linearized Neumann data stably determines the nonlinear coefficients provided that, at any given time, they are known in some neighborhood of the boundary. The proof relies on linearization and complex geometric optics (CGO) solutions for the linear Schrödinger equation. We conclude by outlining an approach based on the direct use of Carleman estimates to recover time-independent coefficients in the setting of trivial boundary data but nontrivial initial data.

title: Optimizers for the finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality
abstract: The finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality provides an estimate on the Riesz sum of the first $N$ negative eigenvalues of the fractional Schrödinger operator $(-Δ)^s-V$ in terms of the $L^{γ+\frac{d}{2s}}(\mathbb R^d)$ norm of the potential $V$, where the Riesz exponent $γ>\max\left\{0,1-d/(2s)\right\}$. We prove the existence of optimizers for every finite rank by establishing a result on the spectrum in the case of dichotomy. We further characterize the spectral gap and qualitative properties of optimizers, including the Euler--Lagrange equation, regularity, and asymptotic behavior at infinity. In particular, under the condition $γ+{d}/{(2s)}\geq 3+{4s}/{d}$, we show that all normalized maximizing sequences are precompact modulo translations. Moreover, we derive a strict binding inequality for the optimal constants in the finite-rank setting, which implies that the optimal fractional Lieb--Thirring constant, if it exists, cannot be attained by a potential with finitely many negative eigenvalues.

title: The $L\log L$-Luxemburg Discrepancy for Nonnegative Weights Suffers from the Curse of Dimensionality
abstract: We study the normalized discrepancy in the Luxemburg norm generated by $Φ(s)=s\log(1+s)$. For arbitrary nonnegative quadrature weights, we prove that the associated information complexity suffers from the curse of dimensionality: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there exist constants $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $d_0=d_0(\varepsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that \[N_{Φ,+}(\varepsilon,d)\ge c_{\varepsilon} d^{-1}(1.07735\ldots)^d \qquad \mbox{for all } d\ge d_0. \] The result therefore also applies to equal-weight quasi-Monte Carlo rules.

title: Bond-informed search for ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys
abstract: Ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) control their local structure and influence a broad range of mechanical and thermodynamic properties. Yet they are notoriously difficult to identify. Locating low-energy ordered candidates requires exploring a configurational space that grows combinatorially with the number of elements, and Monte Carlo searches driven by density-functional theory (DFT) need a new electronic-structure calculation at every trial step. Here we introduce MECx (Minimum Energy Configuration eXplorer), a framework that guides Monte Carlo searches with a surrogate energy model trained on configurations stratified in bond-count space. Applied to ternary, quaternary, and quinary BCC alloys using compact training sets of 100 DFT-labeled configurations, MECx identifies ordered configurations with lower energies than those found by direct DFT-based Monte Carlo within practical computational limits. These configurations exhibit distinct pair-specific ordering, including B2- and B32-like motifs, and undergo progressive disordering as temperature increases. The MPEA-trained models also transfer to selected binary subsystems without retraining. The resulting ordered configurations agree with those obtained by direct DFT-based Monte Carlo and produce experimentally distinguishable superlattice reflections in simulated neutron diffraction patterns.

title: International Multi-Centre Validation of Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Precise Discrimination between Normal and Abnormal Retinal Development
abstract: Arrested retinal development can cause childhood visual impairment, but grading optical coherence tomography scans is difficult to standardise across devices and centres. We developed and evaluated an unsupervised domain adaptation model to classify normal and abnormal retinal development across different OCT systems. This retrospective multicentre study used OCT scans from five centres in four countries and the UK Biobank. Data covered four OCT devices, including table mounted and handheld systems. A ResNet50 based Domain Adversarial Neural Network was trained using labelled images from a source device and unlabelled images from a target device. We evaluated six source to target pairings and compared model performance with seven clinician graders. A separate Heidelberg Spectralis dataset was reserved for external evaluation. Across validation sets, accuracy ranged from 87.75% to 96.06%, sensitivity from 88.68% to 98.38%, and specificity from 78.00% to 98.02%. The best performing model, adapted from TM OCT1 to HH OCT1, achieved 96.06% accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.994, with a 95% confidence interval from 0.981 to 0.999. Several models also maintained discrimination on the unseen Heidelberg device. Unsupervised domain adaptation enabled OCT classification across devices without labelled target device data. The approach may support more consistent assessment of retinal development and large scale analysis of existing imaging datasets.

title: FIRM: Fisher-Informed Retention Merging for Federated LLM Unlearning
abstract: Federated LLM unlearning addresses targeted knowledge removal when forget and retain data remain distributed across private clients and are inaccessible to the server. The resulting locally trained adapters encode conflicting objectives, making their aggregation fundamentally different from conventional federated optimization. A key failure mode is magnitude explosion, whereby unnormalized cross-client aggregation increases the merged update magnitude and degrades retained utility under stronger unlearning. We propose FIRM (Fisher-Informed Retention Merging), a single-round framework for stable and retention-aware server-side aggregation. FIRM uses client-local Fisher statistics as a unified sensitivity signal to construct a Fisher-normalized base merge and impose explicit control over retain-sensitive parameters. Its second-order retention projection admits a unique minimum-distance solution, while the corresponding dual scales with the number of retain clients rather than the model dimension. Experiments across WMDP, TOFU, and MUSE-HP using Zephyr-7B and Llama-3-8B show utility gains at comparable forgetting on WMDP and MUSE-HP, with metric-dependent trade-offs on TOFU. Controlled comparisons support benefits of the combined base merge and additional retention correction at selected operating points.

title: Stability analysis of the steady solution for incompressible lid-driven cavity flow
abstract: Steady solutions at high Reynolds numbers are computed using an iterative method that linearizes the nonlinear convective terms. This linearization reduces the original nonlinear boundary-value problem to a sequence of linear problems, one solved at each iteration, thereby improving the numerical robustness of the algorithm and enabling convergence over a wide range of governing parameters. The stability of steady incompressible fluid flows is studied within the framework of a linear problem for perturbations. The original steady velocity and pressure fields are subjected to small perturbations, after which the equations are linearized with respect to the perturbations. The resulting linear problem allows one to analyze the evolution of small perturbations and to establish whether the steady solutions under consideration are stable with respect to infinitesimal perturbations. In this work, the computational implementation is based on spatial discretization by the finite element method on triangular meshes. The stability of the obtained solutions is analyzed by solving a generalized algebraic eigenvalue problem formed after discretization of the linear problem for perturbations. The presence of eigenvalues with positive real part indicates instability, whereas their absence indicates stability. Calculations were performed on a sequence of refined meshes at various Reynolds numbers for the flow in a square cavity.

title: Hydrostatic Equilibrium Constraints on the Fuzzy Dark Matter Mass from Dwarf Spheroidals: Method, Systematics, and Robustness
abstract: We present the analysis of a non-parametric estimator of the fuzzy (wave) dark matter (FDM) boson mass based on local hydrostatic equilibrium: the classical gravitational acceleration must be balanced by the gradient of the quantum potential of the Schrödinger-Poisson-Madelung system. We apply this condition, without assuming a soliton or any other parametric profile, to the non-parametric density and enclosed mass posteriors from pyGravSphere of the nine Milky Way dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxies. For each posterior realization we solve, in a least squares sense over a fixed radial window, for the boson mass that best balances the two terms, which yields a posterior distribution of mass for each galaxy. The per galaxy medians span $m\sim(0.8$-$4.6)\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{eV}$, with Draco and Ursa Minor the lightest and Carina and Sextans the heaviest. A weighted mass estimate gives $m=(1.3\pm3.5)\times10^{-20}$ eV, dominated by Draco and Ursa Minor. We characterize the systematics in detail.

title: Operator-Space Entanglement Entropy in Random Fermionic Gaussian Dynamics
abstract: We study the von Neumann operator-space entanglement entropy (OSEE) of initial product operators evolved under random gaussian dynamics, as modeled by a Brownian SYK$_2$ model. By exploiting a mapping to a domain-wall melting problem, we derive an exact expression for the time-dependent bipartite OSEE in the thermodynamic limit, and obtain an analytic characterization of the corresponding gaussian Page curve emerging at late times. Our results build on recent work on the entanglement dynamics in the all-to-all quantum simple exclusion process, leveraging tools from RMT, including the Coulomb-gas approach and a mapping to the free Jacobi process. Finally, based on our results, we discuss the possibility of relating the OSEE with non-gaussianity measures in the Heisenberg picture.

title: Graphs with three eigenvalues from group divisible designs
abstract: We construct biregular graphs with three distinct eigenvalues from semiregular group divisible designs. For every prime power $q$, we use the spectral structure of Muzychuk's Construction~A on $q+1$ copies of $\operatorname{AG}(2,q^2)$ to produce suitable group divisible designs. The resulting biregular graphs have $2q^5+q^4+q^2$ vertices and distinct eigenvalues $q^5+q^3+q^2$, $q^2$, and $-q^2$. Their coherent closures have rank $12$ and type $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}3&2\\2&5\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. We also determine the four-class symmetric association schemes that are the coherent closures of the auxiliary graphs in this family. Computational searches provide further graphs on $81$ and $156$ vertices, using Muzychuk's Construction~B and a generalised quadrangle, respectively; their coherent closures have ranks $13$ and $10$. The $156$-vertex example has a strongly regular design as its coherent closure, of type $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}3&2\\2&3\end{smallmatrix}\right]$, answering a question of the authors. We also realise a $126$-vertex example by switching a strongly regular graph.

title: Bézout bounds and rational points on quasianalytic graphs
abstract: For functions $f : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ in quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes $\mathcal C_M$, we establish explicit bounds for the number of intersection points of the graph $Γ(f)$ with algebraic curves of degree at most $d$. The bounds are given in terms of the Bang degree determined by the weight sequence $M$, the degree $d$, and the norming constant of $Γ(f)$ with respect to the space of real bivariate polynomials of degree at most $d$. We give instances, where the bounds are at most polynomial in $d$ and, consequently, the graph $Γ(f)$ contains few rational points: the number of rational points of height at most $H$ is bounded by a polynomial in $\log H$.

title: Fisher Information and Support Complexity of Gaussian Mixtures
abstract: We study lower bounds on the Fisher information of Gaussian location mixtures and their applications to estimation problems. First, for a discrete mixing distribution, we derive a universal positive-semidefinite lower bound on the Fisher information matrix in terms of the Rényi entropy of order two. For a mixing distribution supported on $K$ points, this bound scales as $\log(K)/K^2$, improving by a logarithmic factor on the support-size dependence obtained from Stam's inequality. We then develop dimension-aware trace bounds using classical Sobolev inequalities. These bounds are expressed in terms of Sibson's $α$-mutual information and yield the scaling $K^{-2/n}$ in dimension $n$. A complementary bound involving the $α$-mutual information of order $1/2$ is obtained using the sharp Young convolution inequality. The derived inequalities are further specialized to rotationally invariant mixing distributions supported on discrete spherical shells. In this setting, an intrinsic-dimensional bound on Sibson mutual information leads to lower bounds on the Fisher information in terms of the number of occupied shells. As applications, we study least favorable priors for bounded Gaussian mean estimation. In the scalar case, we show that the least favorable prior on $[-R,R]$ has at least $Ω(R\sqrt{\log R})$ support points and that each of its probability masses is of order at most $1/R$. In the vector case, we show that the number of occupied shells grows at least linearly with $R$. Finally, Brown's identity and the I-MMSE relationship are used to translate the Fisher-information inequalities into upper bounds on the MMSE and mutual information.

title: Only their cardinality can prevent groups from being quotients of weakly branch groups
abstract: It is a well-known fact that every proper quotient of a branch group is a virtually abelian group. We record that every group of cardinality at most $2^{\aleph_0}$ is a quotient of a weakly branch group; in fact, there are weakly branch groups that are split extensions with free complements. Furthermore, if a group is generated by $d$ elements, there is a weakly branch group generated by $(d+2)$ elements mapping onto it. As applications of this fact, we resolve a question of Thillaisundaram on the existence of weakly branch but non-branch groups with maximal subgroups of infinite index and, partially, a question of Cox and Thillaisundaram on the existence of weakly branch groups that are not invariably generated.

title: Resolutions of compact balanced spaces
abstract: Let $X$ be a compact reduced balanced complex space of pure dimension $n\geq2$. We prove that every resolution of singularities of $X$ is a balanced manifold; in particular, $X$ belongs to the class $\mathscr{B}$. This removes the additional cohomological assumptions appearing in earlier results of Fu-Meng-Xia. The main new ingredient is the linear independence of the Aeppli classes of the exceptional prime divisors of a projective bimeromorphic morphism onto a normal complex space. This follows from the vanishing of curve degrees for Aeppli-trivial divisors and the relative negativity lemma. For non-normal spaces, strict positivity is used to eliminate divisors mapping onto codimension-one subsets before passing to the normalization. We also recall a classical surface example of Grauert showing that the inclusion of compact balanced spaces in $\mathscr{B}$ is strict.

title: Short-Boundary Signaling for Asynchronous Grant-Free Control-to-Control Communications
abstract: In asynchronous grant-free access, receivers must detect variable-length transmissions and identify their start and end. Existing decoder-aided receivers use start and tail sequences which are as long as one codeword, causing substantial overhead for short commands. This paper treats the boundary (i.e., start and tail sequences) length as an independent design parameter and proposes a convolutional neural network that detects both boundaries from the received waveform and the decoder soft output. Its waveform input size decreases with the boundary length, while the decoder input keeps the codeword length, so the boundary can be shortened without altering the decoder. Analysis and simulations quantify the resulting tradeoff among payload efficiency, collision exposure, and boundary detection. The results show that the proposed receiver can exploit very short boundaries: in the considered setting, the shortest tested boundary, $L_{\mathrm{b}}=16$, yields the highest effective payload efficiency at all tested loads, whereas a correlation-based benchmark with the same sequences performs best with $L_{\mathrm{b}}=64$ at moderate and high loads.

title: A New Bound for the Gauss Circle Problem
abstract: Let $E(X)=\#\{(a,b)\in\Z^2:a^2+b^2\le X\}-πX$. We prove that $E(X)=O_\varepsilon(X^{209/670+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, uniformly for real $X\ge4$. This breaks the $5/16$ threshold suggested by Huxley as a possible limit of the Bombieri--Iwaniec method at the time. The proof introduces two refinements: a cone distribution estimate that preserves separate fourth- and sixth-power contributions in the double large sieve, and an explicit inversion of Taylor-coefficient constraints that cancels the linear error in a pair-counting argument. These refinements, together with the Robert--Sargos and Watt spacing estimates and the Vinogradov mean value theorem, yield the improvement.

title: Retrieved but Not Read: Understanding Why Search-Augmented LLMs Fail to Use Available Evidence
abstract: Web search allows LLMs to access up-to-date information, but it remains unclear why they sometimes produce outdated answers even when relevant evidence is available. To study this problem, we construct temporal facts whose values changed after the models' training cutoffs. We evaluate one proprietary model under deployed web search and six open-weight model configurations under controlled retrieval. We find that models often answer from search snippets without opening the source pages, which is associated with higher rates of outdated answers and unfaithful citations. Our controlled experiments and layer-wise analysis reveal a gap between the availability of evidence and its effective use. Even when retrieved evidence influences internal predictions, models may still favour outdated information in their final answers. We hope these findings will help advance research on the reliable use of retrieved evidence in search-augmented LLMs.

title: A multi-point maximum principle to prove the global Harnack inequality for the doubly nonlinear heat equation
abstract: This work aims to present a new proof of the global pointwise Harnack inequality satisfied by positive viscosity solutions of the doubly nonlinear heat equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Our approach is based on a multi-point maximum principle argument introduced by the authors in a recent article [Calc. Var., 2026]. Required for the proof is a new variation of the maximum principle for semicontinuous functions, which is a standard tool in the analysis of viscosity solutions. In particular, our techniques provide a new proof of the Harnack inequalities satisfied by positive solutions of the porous medium equation and the $p$-heat equation, which were derived by Auchmuty and Bao [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., 1994] using results of Aronson and Bénilan [C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris, 1979] and Esteban and Vázquez [Arch. Rational Mech. Anal., 1988]. The results contained in this article have also been discussed in the third author's doctoral thesis.

title: Low magnon damping of a EuSe film down to millikelvin temperatures
abstract: The rapid development of quantum magnonics over the past decade has created a demand for magnetic materials that keep their magnon losses low at millikelvin temperatures and add functionality beyond that of the established iron garnets and ferromagnetic metals. The europium chalcogenides are natural candidates $-$ they are magnetic semiconductors whose moment of $7\,μ_{\mathrm{B}}$ per Eu$^{2+}$ ion stems from a half-filled $4f$ shell with zero orbital momentum, so that spin-orbit coupling and intrinsic damping are expected to be weak. Here we characterize an epitaxial film of the metamagnet EuSe on diamagnetic BaF$_2$ by magnetometry and broadband ferromagnetic resonance from 10 K down to 30 mK. EuSe combines a saturation magnetization of 1100 kA/m with antiferromagnetic, ferrimagnetic and ferromagnetic phases that are reached with fields below 0.25 T. In contrast to a Gilbert-damped ferromagnet, the linewidth of the field-aligned film decreases with increasing frequency and field, and below 750 mK it no longer depends on temperature. At 30 mK, 68 GHz and 1.8 T, it reaches 5.5 mT, close to the values of bulk single crystals, which corresponds to a magnon lifetime of 2 ns and to an upper bound of $1.1\times10^{-3}$ for the Gilbert damping parameter. These properties make EuSe and the europium chalcogenides promising materials for hybrid quantum systems and quantum magnonics.

title: A sharp criterion for well-posedness of semilinear Schrödinger equations on the real line
abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semilinear Schrödinger equations on the real line. We establish a sharp necessary and sufficient condition on the nonlinearity for local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces of regularity greater than five halves. This criterion is formulated in terms of the Mizohata condition and is equivalent to explicit algebraic conditions on the nonlinearity. To prove sufficiency, we combine energy estimates with a gauge transformation adapted to the bounded primitive arising from the Mizohata condition. To prove necessity, we show that the failure of the condition yields a dense set of initial data for which no solution exists on any positive time interval.

title: Uni-PNP: Unified Prehensile and Non-prehensile Policy Learning for Generalizable Object Pose Reaching
abstract: Object manipulation often requires combining non-prehensile actions with grasping. However, existing approaches typically develop these capabilities separately and integrate them by sequencing distinct primitives through prescribed intermediate objectives, limiting the coordination of contact motions and grasping. Their integration also remains sensitive to object and gripper geometry and depends on particular environmental supports, complicating real-world deployment. We present Uni-PNP, a unified policy that jointly learns prehensile and non-prehensile manipulation for object pose reaching across diverse objects and grippers. To achieve this, we first pretrain a geometry encoder to predict contact-induced object motion using a contact-dynamics dataset constructed from simulated interactions between diverse objects and grippers. We then train the policy in a two-stage reinforcement learning curriculum from graspable objects to ungraspable peers, encouraging the discovery of non-prehensile interactions and their integration with grasping. Experiments show 76.39% success on hundreds of seen objects with grippers, and 57.91% on unseen peers, outperforming the strongest pose-reaching baseline by 20.52 and 17.79 percentage points, respectively. We also analyze emergent behaviors, including nonprehensile and prehensile repositioning, grasp acquisition that requires grasping after tipping, and table-assisted reorientation while grasping, and transfer to the real-world scenario. Project page available at lgswdn.github.io/Uni-PNP.

title: In-Context Preference-Conditioned Pareto Set Learning from Limited Offline Data
abstract: Multi-objective optimization involves diverse preferences over conflicting objectives. Rather than returning a finite set of trade-off solutions, preference-conditioned Pareto set learning seeks to map a specified preference directly to a corresponding Pareto optimal solution. Yet in many real-world scenarios, optimization must proceed offline without further objective evaluations, leaving only a limited static dataset that sparsely covers the decision and objective spaces. Existing methods either optimize separately for each preference or train a problem-specific Pareto solution model, requiring repeated search across preferences or repeated training across problems. We introduce in-context preference-conditioned Pareto set learning (ICPSL), a framework that amortizes both preference-wise solution search and problem-specific model construction. ICPSL pretrains a foundation-style hypernetwork on a large and diverse set of synthetic prior data. Given the offline observations of an unseen problem, the pretrained hypernetwork learns to generate a problem-specific, preference-conditioned Pareto solution model in a single forward pass. The generated model can then be reused to predict solutions for arbitrary preferences without problem-specific training or preference-wise search. Experiments on synthetic and real-world problems show that ICPSL produces high-quality Pareto solutions while providing substantial speedups in problem-specific solution-model construction.

title: SceneWeave: Audience-Guided Scene Exploration for Dramatic Adaptation
abstract: Adapting prose into a script requires transforming narration and inner experience into scenes that convey relationships and psychological contradictions. Planning specifies intended effects but leaves their realization in dialogue and action unresolved. Drawing on screenwriters' accounts of revising scenes and their connections to the surrounding work, we present SceneWeave, which uses alternative scene drafts to revise the adaptation as a whole. It writes contrasting treatments of a focal scene, compares the interactions they create, and revises characterization, preceding preparation, subsequent development, and scene order before generating the complete script. The central contribution is to use actual scene writing to inform adaptation decisions and propagate their consequences across the work. We also develop a task-specific writing model and a human-preference model for comparing script drafts. The writing model learns from adaptation examples and human preferences; the preference model combines human and synthetic supervision. Blind reader comparisons favor SceneWeave over a baseline workflow and description-based controls, while content assessment indicates reduced narrative redundancy and strong psychological treatment.

title: Local definable $(p,q)$-theorem and a refinement
abstract: We prove the definable $(p,q)$-conjecture for NIP formulas in arbitrary first-order theories. We also prove a refinement and apply it to dense pairs.

title: Reliable Knowledge Acquisition for Continual Learning Agents
abstract: As agents powered by foundation models move into open-ended environments, continual learning from experience becomes essential. For agents built on models with fixed parameters, this learning requires reusing prior task experience in context to improve performance and efficiency on future tasks. Existing memory and experience-learning systems typically focus on either retained facts or procedures, and lack a mechanism for establishing the reliability of claims extracted from the ongoing task stream. Indeed, we find that approximately 12--33\% of entries produced by representative systems harm future task performance when reused. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{RIKA} (Reliable Knowledge Acquisition), which combines hierarchical extraction of factual, conceptual, procedural, and metacognitive knowledge with Evidence-based Knowledge Admission, which uses source evidence and subsequent experience to govern which claims enter the task agent's context, without additional validation tasks. Across six task streams from Continual Learning Bench and four model backbones, RIKA achieves the highest aggregate score on every backbone.

title: An IMEX multi-level domain-decomposition method for the Boltzmann equation on unstructured meshes
abstract: We introduce a dynamically adaptive multi-level method for the multiscale Boltzmann equation on unstructured meshes, coupling the compressible Euler, Navier-Stokes, and full Boltzmann descriptions within a single asymptotic-preserving IMEX framework. Unlike standard domain-decomposition approaches, where independent solvers exchange data only through interface conditions, the three models form a unified multiregime scheme. They share the same globally stiffly accurate IMEX Runge-Kutta discretization and are synchronized at every internal stage through kinetic-to-fluid moment projections and fluid-to-kinetic lifting. This stage-wise coupling maintains temporal consistency across model interfaces, while the asymptotic-preserving structure ensures compatibility with the fluid limit as the Knudsen number becomes small. The active description is selected in each cell through moment-realizability indicators derived from successive Chapman-Enskog approximations. The hierarchy uses Euler in near-equilibrium regions, Navier-Stokes where first-order nonequilibrium corrections are sufficient, and the full Boltzmann equation where a kinetic description is required. Using Navier-Stokes as the intermediate level avoids evolving a velocity distribution in mildly nonequilibrium regions, which is particularly advantageous on unstructured meshes, where kinetic transport dominates the cost. The spatial discretization combines finite-volume WENO reconstruction on triangular meshes with a conservative fast spectral method for the Boltzmann collision operator. Numerical experiments show that the method closely reproduces the full Boltzmann reference while significantly reducing the computational cost. These results suggest that tightly coupled AP model hierarchies are a viable alternative to interface-based domain decomposition for deterministic kinetic simulations in complex geometries.

title: Comfortably Stuck: Evaluation Pitfalls in Bench2Drive's Closed-Loop Protocol
abstract: Closed-loop evaluation is widely regarded as a more faithful way to assess end-to-end (E2E) driving models than open-loop evaluation, and Bench2Drive, built on the CARLA simulator, has become the dominant benchmark for it. We show that its evaluation protocol itself contains pitfalls that can misrepresent the models scored on it. Bench2Drive's comfort metric, adapted from nuPlan, has several implementation errors and a segmentation scheme that rewards standing still, so it mostly measures how long a vehicle stays stationary, correlating with stationary time at r = 0.97 across eight models. We propose a corrected, distance-based metric that cuts that correlation to r = 0.06. Under it, the strong driving-score/comfort tradeoff the original metric reports is no longer detectable once models are compared at matched driving speed, which suggests that comfort trades against how fast a model drives rather than against how well it drives. We also uncover two pitfalls in how the harness supplies navigation signals: the default controller can replace a model's own steering with an angle toward the route target point, and the target point supplied at evaluation time can differ substantially from what a model saw in training. We demonstrate both on UniAD and VAD, where their effects differ sharply, and argue that future closed-loop evaluations should check for them. We will release all fixes as standalone code, so corrected comfort scores can be obtained from logged trajectories without re-running closed-loop simulation.

title: Sparse Federated Echo State Networks for Time-Series Classification via Smooth-L1 Regularization
abstract: Echo State Networks (ESNs), as lightweight implementations of reservoir computing, provide efficient solutions for temporal data processing in resource-constrained environments. While standard ESNs offer computational efficiency, their dense readout layers inflate the stored model and the per-sample inference cost. This paper introduces a Smooth-L1 regularized ESN (SL1ESN) that promotes sparsity in the readout layer while preserving differentiability for gradient-based optimization. The method employs a twice-differentiable Smooth-L1 approximation compatible with Newton's method, which we exploit both for centralized training and for a second-order (Newton-step) federated aggregation scheme. Under a single fixed shrinkage threshold shared by every dataset and both settings, experiments on seven time-series classification benchmarks show that SL1ESN learns readouts that are $77$--$95\%$ sparse in the centralized setting and $75$--$95\%$ sparse in the federated one, while staying within $0.7$ accuracy points of the strongest dense baseline on five of the seven benchmarks in the centralized setting and within $1.6$ points on the same five in the federated one, and the second-order federated update converges in only a few rounds. The resulting sparsity compresses the stored model, the per-sample inference cost, and the server-to-client broadcast by a comparable factor. These results demonstrate the practical value of sparse readouts for edge computing and IoT deployments.

title: Pairwise AUC Optimization Needs Corrective Power: A Unified View
abstract: Direct pairwise AUC-surrogate training is attractive because it trains toward the ranking metric used at test time, especially under class imbalance. This creates a direct alignment between the training objective and the evaluation metric, but such metric alignment alone does not guarantee that stochastic training remains corrective. We study this gap through Corrective Power: whether pairwise mini-batch updates produce stronger and more reliable improvements for more severe positive-negative ranking errors. Our main observation is that direct pairwise training can enter regions where severe errors remain common but no longer produce useful corrective motion. In such regions, even the mini-batch noise that would normally help SGD move along the steepest severe-error correction direction can become much weaker. In this paper, we seek a theoretical explanation for this by exploring the degenerate property of the U-statistics formed from the pairwise gradients therein. Our results provide a mechanistic explanation for several empirical patterns: (a) squared-hinge loss is often an effective AUC surrogate; (b) cross-entropy warm-up can help models that enter the AUC phase from a poor starting region; and (c) parameter-efficient fine-tuning from a pretrained model can reduce that need by starting closer to a favorable ranking geometry. Experiments on 8 CV tasks and 8 NLP tasks, using ResNet50, DenseNet121, DistilBERT-base, and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, support these predictions.

title: Benchmarking Priors: A Fully Bayesian Approach to Small Area Benchmarking
abstract: We develop a new class of priors for Bayesian small area models under strict external bench- marking constraints. The prior is fully supported on the constrained parameter set defined by the benchmarking constraints and thereby provides a proper constrained posterior that is fully supported on the restricted set. The posterior naturally constrains the small area estimates to conform to the benchmarking values at the aggregate level. In addition, it facilitates valid uncertainty quantification using credible sets that are fully contained within the constrained set. This novel framework has a wide range of applicability, ranging from the standard Gaus- sian Fay-Herriot model to more general Fay-Herriot models, such as robust Fay-Herriot models, where the area-level random effects are distributed as multivariate t, or Fay-Herriot models where there is a complex nonlinear relationship between the area means and the covariates. We illustrate the usefulness of the proposed methodology using simulation experiments as well as by estimating the state-level proportion of children aged 5-17 living under poverty based on the direct estimates obtained from the Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (SAIPE) program of the U.S. Census Bureau and the national benchmark of the child poverty rate obtained from the Annual Social and Economic Supplement of the Current Population Survey (CPS ASEC) conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau. The numerical results reaffirm the advantages of the proposed benchmarking priors.

title: Moment Propagation for the Vlasov--Poisson System with Gyroscopic Forces, Velocity Diffusion, and Specular Reflection
abstract: This paper studies the three-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with gyroscopic forces and velocity diffusion. For the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^3$ and the specular--Dirichlet problem in bounded domains, we prove the propagation of velocity moments of order $k>2$ for weak solutions with bounded $L^1\cap L^{\infty}$ norms and kinetic energy. The proof applies Serre's compensated integrability to weighted mass--momentum tensors to derive density estimates. A finite iteration alternating moment propagation with improved density integrability then closes the estimates. These estimates provide a simplified approach to moment propagation and yield global continuation of classical solutions.

title: The Delegation Dilemma: Economies of Scale, Accountability, and Polycentric Governance
abstract: Many collective-action systems are neither fully decentralized nor fully centralized: agents voluntarily organize into institutions that share organizational costs and delegate decisions to representatives. Delegation can reduce individual costs, but it also transfers control to representatives whose private objectives need not align with those of their constituents. We study this tension in a repeated game with endogenous delegation to self-interested centers. A simple reduced-form model yields a scale--accountability tradeoff: larger constituencies offer greater cost-sharing benefits to members, yet the marginal value to a center of retaining any one constituent decreases as group size grows. Consequently, the prospect of individual exit can sustain non-exploitative delegation only up to an endogenous accountable constituency size. Additionally, we identify parameter regions in which fully delegated, accountable governance, when feasible, must be polycentric. We investigate these predictions through simulations with large language model (LLM) agents. Across five matched pairs of 30-agent simulations, polycentric structures repeatedly emerge but remain fluid, exhibiting cycles of concentration, exploitation, exit, and re-formation. We further find that models of different capacity exhibit similar willingness to assume leadership but differ substantially in their exercise of authority, with Sol initiating exploitation more frequently than Luna in matched decision states.

title: On a critical curl-curl system of Lane-Emden type
abstract:
We study the system $

abla	imes

We prove the existence of a ground state solution by reducing the system to a quasilinear fourth-order curl-curl equation and minimizing the associated Sobolev-curl quotient. A concentration-compactness argument shows there are finitely many concentration points for a Palais-Smale sequence $(u_n)$. This yields a.e. convergence of $
abla	imes

If $p=q$, we show $u$ and $v$ are necessarily equal for every solution. In an appendix we show that our concentration argument also applies to a scalar quasilinear fourth order equation.

title: The Dormant Spiking Neuron: A State-Driven Mechanism for Efficient Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer a compelling pathway toward energy-efficient artificial intelligence, fundamentally anchored in presynaptic input-driven sparsity. However, a substantial yet chronically overlooked source of computational overhead persists: the continuous subthreshold dynamics of postsynaptic neurons. Quantitative analysis reveals that up to 44% of neurons in an ImageNet-trained ResNet-18 model reside in a deeply inhibited state, imposing a persistent computational burden despite having a negligible probability of firing. To address this inefficiency, the Dormant Spiking Neuron (DSN) model is introduced. By incorporating a state-driven dynamic gate, the DSN allows a neuron to enter a dormant state when its membrane potential falls below a predefined negative threshold, dynamically pruning redundant computations at the instance level. Crucially, this dormancy mechanism is directly integrated into the neuronal dynamics and trained end-to-end via backpropagation through time using surrogate gradients, enabling the network to actively learn a robust dormancy policy that adaptively preserves critical information flow. Extensive experiments across static and neuromorphic datasets demonstrate that the DSN framework consistently reduces computational energy by 40% to over 70%. Notably, on the large-scale ImageNet dataset, the DSN outperforms state-of-the-art static pruning techniques at comparable reported cost reductions and simultaneously improves the corresponding baseline SNN accuracy by 1.34%. By establishing a trainable, state-driven sparsity paradigm orthogonal to conventional input-driven methods, the DSN unlocks synergistic efficiency gains, presenting an effective approach for advancing neuromorphic computing.

title: Pseudoconvex domains in complex Euclidean space with one-dimensional Bergman spaces
abstract: For any $n \geq 2$, we construct a pseudoconvex domain in $\C^n$ such that the Bergman space is one-dimensional. This disproves Wiegerinck conjecture.

title: Harmful Partial Interventions and Benign Leakage in Concept-based Models
abstract: Artificial intelligence systems deployed in high-risk settings increasingly require models that support meaningful human oversight. Concept-based models (CMs) offer a promising framework by enabling users to inspect and intervene on intermediate, human-understandable concepts. However, concept interventions can counterintuitively worsen downstream predictions, a failure mode we formalise as intervention harm. We distinguish harm after all concepts have been intervened on from harm under partial interventions, the more likely practical use case. Modern CMs often achieve high accuracy by encoding, or leaking, additional task-relevant information in their intermediate concept representations. Recent work argues that such leakage can be benign with respect to intervention harm when concept representations satisfy two conditions: sufficiency and localisation. We prove that these criteria are not sufficient to guarantee that concept interventions improve downstream performance. Across controlled and real-world settings, we find that concept supervision incompleteness is associated with increased intervention harm. Importantly, optimising the model when all concepts are intervened on, a previously proposed leakage mitigation objective, reduces endpoint harm but does not reliably prevent harmful partial corrections. Hence, we introduce a complementary monotonic intervention objective that directly penalises increases in task loss along partial intervention trajectories. Combining endpoint and monotonic intervention training substantially reduces the prevalence and magnitude of partial intervention harm while preserving concept and task predictive performance.

title: Multi-Higgs production from a theory of varying Higgs quartic and top Yukawa couplings
abstract: We study the collider phenomenology of a theory in which the Higgs quartic self-coupling and the top Yukawa coupling are \textit{varying couplings}, which arise dynamically from two scalar fields, $ϕ_1$ and $ϕ_2$. Depending on the scalar masses relative to twice the top-quark mass, the heavy scalars decay mainly to Higgs boson pairs ($hh$) or to top-quark pairs ($t\bar t$), giving two distinct signatures. We find sizeable cross sections for resonant $hh$ production, and also for the background-suppressed process with three Higgs bosons ($hhh$) from associated production, $pp \to hϕ_i \to hhh$. By recasting ATLAS resonance searches, we set bounds on the effective new-physics scales $Λ_1$ and $Λ_2$ at the TeV scale. We also show that the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) will probe this parameter space further, through combined measurements of the $hh$, $t\bar t$ and multi-Higgs channels. This gives a strong, multi-channel test of whether the electroweak sector has a dynamical origin.

title: Quotients of Calabi-Yau Generalized Fermat manifolds and Log Enriques varieties
abstract: Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties have attracted a lot of interest in the last years. In this paper we study Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties that are respectively étale and quasi-étale quotients of Calabi-Yau manifolds. We produce several examples by studying quotients of generalized Fermat manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. These are complete intersections of Fermat type manifolds all of the same degree and were described recently by Hidalgo, Hughes and Leyton-Álvarez. We describe all their quotients by a fixed-point-free automorphism. Most of the quotients are Log Enriques varieties or Calabi-Yau varieties with terminal singularities. In one case we get a family of Enriques manifolds which is a subfamily of a family described previously by Boissière, Camere and the third author, which is one of the two so far known families of Enriques manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. This family is obtained as an étale quotient of order two of a Calabi-Yau manifold complete intersection of quadrics, the other family is the Hilbert scheme of $n$ points on an Enriques surface. In the last part of the paper we show that these two families are different by computing their second Betti numbers, which are equal to one and eleven respectively.

title: Sensing-Assisted OFDM with Index Modulation: A Waveform for Optical Wireless Integrated Communication and Localisation
abstract: This paper proposes sensing-assisted OFDM with index modulation (SA-OFDM-IM) for joint communication and localisation over optical wireless systems. In SA-OFDM-IM, a multilayer frequency-domain architecture partitions each layer's admissible subcarriers into disjoint communication and distributed sensing-pilot subsets, applying group-wise index modulation (IM) within the communication subset. A constrained sensing-to-communication energy allocation jointly minimises average bit-error rate (BER) and delay-based localisation root mean square error (RMSE) under a minimum power-domain margin, enabling low-complexity, ordered-energy detection of both sensing and communication subcarriers without exhaustive maximum-likelihood search. Sensing tones are aggregated across the frame to reconstruct the channel frequency response, yielding the line-of-sight (LoS) delay tap and phase-compensated LoS gain for multilateration and, via the proposed delay-aided received signal strength (RSS) refinement. Simulation results indicate that SA-OFDM-IM can achieve up to 5 dB lower SNR requirement in BER and up to three orders of magnitude lower channel-estimation error than DC-biased optical OFDM, while the RSS estimator removes the SNR-independent error floors of delay-only and hybrid-RSS benchmarks to attain sub-delay-bin range and position accuracy, remaining robust under random known and unknown receiver orientations.

title: Remote Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Entanglement Generation between Trapped Ions
abstract: Distributing entanglement directly between error-corrected logical qubits is an important capability for scalable quantum networks. We propose a heralded protocol for generating remote entanglement between Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill qubits encoded in the motional modes of spatially separated trapped ions, using the internal electronic states to interface the motional qubits with emitted photons. We derive the protocol for single-rail and polarization photonic encodings and evaluate the effects of finite GKP squeezing, photon loss, photon recoil, motional heating, and motional dephasing on the decoded logical state. Moreover, we numerically analysed the fidelity of distributed logical Bell-pair fidelity. We find that one can achieve more than 95% of fidelity in the realistic situation. The protocol combines motional-control and photonic-networking operations that have already been demonstrated in trapped-ion experiments.

title: DeciCAD: Harness-Grounded Learning of Action Policies for CAD Agents
abstract: Large Language Model agents operate through closed-loop action policies whose decision space is defined by an agent harness. We investigate how this operating space shapes agent behavior and policy learning in computer-aided design (CAD), a professional domain characterized by persistent state, geometric constraints, and long-horizon procedures. We instantiate this perspective in DeciCAD, a domain-native harness that exposes semantic CAD actions, decision-oriented observations, environment feedback, and persistent state transitions. Building on this harness, we develop a learning pipeline that extracts causal decision supervision from interaction trajectories and improves the policy through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and geometry-grounded online reinforcement learning (RL). Across four CAD benchmarks, DeciCAD achieves the best F1 and intersection over union (IoU) while reducing model-output tokens by 45--88% relative to a general-purpose coding harness. Under matched supervision, its SFT policy improves F1 from 0.6883 to 0.7437 and outperforms the coding policy; subsequent online RL further raises geometry availability from 66.5% to 73.5% and F1 to 0.7880. These results demonstrate that the decision space induced by a harness materially affects both agent execution and policy learning in CAD.

title: Locally Robust Inference with Outcomes Predicted by Machine Learning
abstract: Many parameters of interest in economics depend on outcomes generated by machine learning (ML).These generated outcomes are subsequently used in standard econometric estimation and typically treated as observed, a practice that threatens the validity of downstream inference. Empirically relevant cases include dynamic treatment effects under sequential exogeneity, long-term effects with surrogates, the partially linear model with an ML-predicted outcome, productivity persistence with an unrestricted production function and constructed instruments, and outcomes residualized of confounding variation. This paper develops a three-step locally robust GMM framework for valid inference when the dependent variable is generated by ML. We construct a debiased moment condition that augments the identifying moment with first- and second-step influence functions, making inference on the parameter of interest locally insensitive to regularization and model selection biases at both steps. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed estimator and illustrate its finite-sample performance through Monte Carlo simulations. We also apply the method to U.S. mortgage data to study conditional Black--White disparities in a race-blind ML default-risk score. The score predicts subsequent default well overall, but the conditional disparity embedded in the score is much smaller than the corresponding disparity in realized serious delinquency; accounting for first-step estimation also raises the naive out-of-sample estimate of the score disparity.

title: Backward stochastic porous media equation with polynomial growth
abstract: We investigate the well-posedness of a backward stochastic porous media equation whose nonlinear term is a polynomial operator corresponding to the slow diffusion regime. The main challenge stems from the structure of this nonlinear operator, which causes the operator to lose maximal monotonicity and prevents the use of standard weak-strong convergence techniques to identify the limit. Moreover, since the Laplace operator makes it difficult to separate the operators and discuss them individually, we attempt to obtain the of limit by investigating the global properties of the operator.

title: Beyond Source Prompts: Towards Visually Grounded AI-Generated Video Quality Assessment
abstract: Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence have accelerated video generation technologies. However, AI-generated videos (AIGVs) remain susceptible to various distortions, highlighting the need for dedicated video quality assessment methods. Content semantics play an important role in AIGV quality assessment, with source prompts typically used as textual references. However, these prompts may not accurately reflect the generated video content, resulting in a discrepancy between the intended textual description and the generated result. To address this limitation, this paper proposes VGCap, an AIGV quality assessment framework guided by visually grounded captions that align better with generated content. Specifically, we introduce two forms of captions: a global caption obtained by minimally revising the source prompt based on multi-frame visual evidence, and prompt-independent segment captions that describe localized temporal content. Together, these captions provide complementary textual evidence for assessing spatial quality, temporal quality, and text-video alignment. Experimental results on the LGVQ and FETV datasets show that VGCap outperforms representative baselines across all three dimensions. Further ablation studies on caption sources and temporal components confirm the effectiveness of visually grounded captions for each quality dimension, while highlighting the benefits of segment-level features for temporal quality prediction. The source of VGCap will be available at https://github.com/lolo123-123/VGCap.

title: Model-Driven Deep Learning for Distributed Detection with Low-Bit Quantization
abstract: Distributed detection plays a fundamental role in communication-efficient collaborative inference over large-scale networks, where spatially distributed nodes must cooperate using severely quantized messages due to bandwidth constraints. While low-bit quantization is essential for reducing communication overhead, it can significantly degrade detection performance, particularly when prior knowledge of observation noise is unavailable. To address this challenge, we propose a model-driven deep learning framework for distributed detection with low-bit quantization. For fixed local quantizers, we first derive the exact finite-sensor maximum a posteriori (MAP) detection error and prove that, under conditionally independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) observations, independent local randomizations, and a common quantization-level constraint, identical quantizers preserve the supremum of the average network Chernoff information. Guided by these results, we develop a binary probabilistic quantizer with a trainable neural probability controller and design a tree-structured probabilistic quantizer for scalable multi-bit quantization. The exact finite-sensor MAP error provides the training objective for the binary quantizer, while we derive a computationally tractable Bhattacharyya surrogate objective for training the multi-bit quantizer. For both cases, we derive analytical MAP fusion rules based on the class-conditional probability mass functions (PMFs) of the quantized messages. When the observation statistics are unknown, these PMFs are estimated from held-out labeled data, yielding plug-in MAP detectors. Simulation results show that the proposed method approaches centralized-oracle performance at higher quantization resolutions and remains effective under changes in network size and test-time signal amplitude.

title: Beyond Generation: Using Multimodal LLMs as Detectors of LLM-Generated Deepfake Facial Images
abstract: As image generation models become increasingly capable of producing highly realistic content, traditional forensic techniques are struggling to keep up. This paper investigates whether MLLMs can instead be used as a form of forensic analysis by identifying synthetic media. Specifically, the study aims to determine whether these models detect fake images by recognising physical inconsistencies, or whether they rely on digital artefacts such as embedded watermarks.Six MLLMs: GPT-4o, GPT-5, GPT-5.2, Gemini 2.5, Gemini 3, and Seed 1.6, are benchmarked using a dataset of 400 images. Fifty images are authentic photographs, while the remaining 350 are generated using seven leading image models: Gemini 3, Gemini 2.5, Flux.2 Pro, GPT-Image-1, GPT-Image-1.5, Seedream 4.0, and Seedream 4.5. The evaluation is structured in three stages: single-image classification, pairwise comparison, and a focused "self-detection" experiment on Gemini. Several MLLMs achieved a high detection accuracy, with GPT-5.2 reaching a peak of 97.9% in the pairwise experiment, against specific generators and an overall mean pairwise accuracy of 82.5% by identifying structural or physical inconsistencies within images. However, results from the self-detection experiment indicate that the presence of invisible SynthID watermarks leads to a 10% reduction in Gemini's detection accuracy compared to the clean control group. One possible explanation is that SynthID embedding reduces some of the visible artefacts the models rely on for detection.These results imply that MLLMs can detect structural artefacts without relying on watermarks, but performance varies substantially across model generations. The findings from comparison C5 also suggest that SynthID embedding may suppress some of the structural artefacts used during detection.

title: Probing Deconfined Quantum Criticality Point on a Digital Quantum Computer
abstract: A deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) is a continuous transition between ordered phases with unrelated broken symmetries, beyond the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm. In one dimension, such a transition between a $z$-polarized ferromagnet (zFM) and a valence-bond solid (VBS) is well established numerically in a frustrated spin-$1/2$ chain. Here we ask whether a superconducting quantum processor can resolve this transition and its signatures despite finite-size effects and device noise. The ground states are prepared by ancilla-projected quantum imaginary-time evolution (QITE), whose exact target states are compressed by tensor-network optimization into shallow depth quantum circuits. The hardware data distinguish the phases through their order parameters, spin and dimer correlations, structure factors, correlation ratios, and snapshot distributions. The crossing of the order parameters locates the transition, and its finite-size extrapolation lies close to the thermodynamic-limit value obtained from large-scale numerics. A noise model based on the device calibration accounts quantitatively for the reduced amplitudes measured on hardware. Our findings demonstrate that a Landau-forbidden transition between competing orders can be resolved on current quantum processors.

title: The linear positive torsor presentation and arithmetic purity of strong approximation
abstract: In this article, we define a notion for varieties called linear positive torsor presentation. For varieties with a linear positive torsor presentation over number fields, we establish the arithmetic purity of strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction off the empty set. As a consequence, we recover arithmetic purity for smooth toric variety with no non-constant global section. Moreover, we classify the chain connected class for rational points on such varieties over any field of characteristic zero.

title: Bias Mitigation in Audio-Enabled LLMs through Adversarial Training and Distillation Methods
abstract: Audio-enabled large language models (AuLLMs) allow users to interact with them simply by talking to them, without the need for an intermediate transcription. This expands the model's accessibility and capabilities by encoding non-verbal cues. However, using non-verbal cues may lead to biased behaviour based on the attributes inferred (or assumed) from them. In this work, we focus on the gender attribute and show that models' perception of it can be unlearned using adversarial methods without a loss in performance on other benchmarked tasks. Such models are useful in situations where gender inference is unwanted. However, in other practical settings, gender perception (without bias) may be desired.As a less radical measure, we distil the gender-agnostic model, creating a model that perceives gender but responds similarly to the gender-agnostic teacher, unless explicitly asked.We apply our newly proposed methods to three AuLLMs and obtain satisfactory results in the gender-unlearning part and partially satisfactory results in the distilling part.

title: Q($γ_H$): Entropy-Guided Horizon Mixing in Multi-Discount Q-Learning
abstract: A fixed discount factor in Q-learning imposes a single planning horizon throughout training, despite the differing demands of early exploration and long-term credit assignment. We propose Q($γ_H$), a multi-horizon Q-learning framework that maintains multiple discount-specific heads and adaptively combines them at control time using an entropy-derived confidence signal. The resulting state-dependent mixing weights shift control from shorter- to longer-horizon heads as policy confidence increases, enabling adaptive horizon mixing without modifying individual Bellman updates. Across classical control and deep reinforcement-learning benchmarks, Q($γ_H$) shows its strongest improvements on delayed-credit tasks relative to strong fixed-discount baselines. By decoupling horizon adaptation from the underlying learning updates, Q($γ_H$) provides a lightweight framework for adaptive planning-horizon control in reinforcement learning, avoiding the need for manual discount-factor selection while remaining compatible with standard value-learning methods.

title: Local finite rate semi device independent randomness expansion from quantum contextuality
abstract: Finite rate randomness expansion (RE) which is secure against quantum adversaries is a crucial information processing task which is well studied in the case of two non-communicating parties sharing Bell non-local correlations in a device independent manner. In this paper we show that contextual correlations with only a single localized party are sufficient for RE in a semi-device independent (SDI) manner. We propose a template SDI-RE protocol which is applicable for arbitrary $N$-cycle non-contextuality (NC) inequalities and derive its RE rate under finite statistics. As a special case, we also highlight the advantages of the situation when RE is constrained by Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality but with characterized measurements implemented by only a single party. Our template protocol also incorporates non-ideal statistics which may not satisfy perfect commutativity and perfect repeatability, both of which are necessary in a loophole-free test of NC inequalities. As such, several recent experimental implementations of significantly loophole-free tests of NC inequalities can be modified for secure RE following our approach.

title: Watt-level single-cavity dual-comb laser at 2.1 $μ$m wavelength
abstract: Compact ultrafast laser combs around the 2 $μ$m atmospheric transmission window are of growing interest for direct spectroscopy and as drivers for nonlinear conversion to otherwise hard-to-reach spectral regions. Dual-comb systems in this region remain very scarce: existing implementations rely mostly on nonlinear conversion, resulting in complex systems with poor conversion efficiency and overall low average and peak power. In this paper, we report on a watt-level dual-comb laser directly emitting at 2.1 $μ$m. The system is based on a single-cavity, soft-aperture Kerr-lens mode-locked (KLM) laser using a broadband holmium (Ho)-doped CaAlGdO$_4$ (CALGO) gain crystal. The laser delivers a total output power exceeding 2 W (1 W per comb) with a sub-100-fs pulse duration (50 nm bandwidth) at a repetition rate of 96.5 MHz, corresponding to a pulse energy of 10 nJ and a peak power of 100 kW per comb. To assess the source's potential for future spectroscopic applications, we characterize the free-running dual comb in detail for frequency stability, phase noise, and relative intensity noise (RIN), and benchmark the achievable spectral resolution by measuring spectral modulations imposed by Fabry-Pérot etalons. Our system combines the compactness, high efficiency, and passive mutual coherence of a single-cavity oscillator with watt-level average power at 2.1 $μ$m, making it a promising source for environmental sensing in the atmospheric transmission window, or as a driver for nonlinear frequency conversion, for example, to the MIR and THz regions.

title: From Research Goals to Scientific Closure: Evaluating Agents Through Evidence-Supported Physics Research
abstract: Can AI agents organize scientific investigations that lead to well-supported conclusions? To evaluate this capability, we introduce PhysClosureBench, a benchmark of 50 expert-verified, goal-specified research tasks spanning strong-field, attosecond, and neighboring physics areas. Each task specifies the research objective and essential scientific constraints, while leaving the agent to organize the investigation and determine how to generate and validate the evidence needed to answer the question. A 20-criterion Atomic Score measures local scientific accomplishment, while Research Closure (RC0--RC4) assesses how fully the investigation resolves the specified research question based on whether its indispensable evidence requirements and applicable scope conditions are satisfied. We evaluate seven frontier LLMs, where Claude-Opus-5 achieves the highest mean Atomic Score (6.29/10) but reaches RC4 in only 32.7% of attempts. Across the benchmark, 36.2% of attempts scoring at least 8/10 still fall short of RC4, while all seven models reach RC4 on substantially fewer tasks in all three runs than in at least one. Case-level analysis further illustrates how misinterpretation of generated results and unresolved physical applicability limits can lead to incomplete closure. Together, these results reveal a persistent gap between AI agents' local scientific accomplishments and their ability to achieve complete research closure.

title: Visible parts and projections of the affine fractal percolation
abstract: We study the visible parts and orthogonal projections of the affine fractal percolation. We show that for the affine fractal percolation $E$, conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, almost surely the dimension of the visible part is equal to $\min\{1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ from all directions except for the major contracting direction. The visible part from the major contracting direction is notably different from the other directions, and we provide a formula for its Hausdorff and box dimensions. In addition, we show that almost surely conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, $\dim_{\rm H} π(E) =\min\{ 1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ for every orthogonal projection $π$ excluding the one onto the major contracting direction, and given $\dim_{\rm H} E >1$, these projections contain intervals.

title: Spatiotemporally correlated activity regulation of random-organizing hyperuniform states
abstract: Center-of-mass (COM) conservation has been widely accepted as an important mechanism for generating nonequilibrium dynamic hyperuniform states with vanishing long-wavelength density fluctuations, but whether it is sufficient for hyperuniformity remains unclear. Here, using particle simulations and a linear fluctuating theory, we show that spatiotemporally correlated activity regulation can destroy hyperuniformity while preserving COM conservation. We construct a binary mixture in which the local density of independently evolving driver particles regulates the activity of regulated particles following COM-conserving biased random organization. This counterexample demonstrates that hyperuniformity depends on the spatial and temporal correlations of activity as well as the conservation laws governing particle displacements. Our findings clarify the limits of COM conservation as a route to hyperuniformity and highlight the importance of controlling activity correlations in the design of nonequilibrium multihyperuniform mixtures.

title: Coexistence of Altermagnetic and Compensated Ferrimagnetic Motifs in a Noncollinear Multiferroic
abstract: Collinear compensated magnets with nonrelativistic spin splitting comprise altermagnets (ALMs), whose rotation- or mirror-related opposite-spin sublattices produce momentum-selective splitting that vanishes at $Γ$, and compensated ferrimagnets (CFIMs), whose symmetry-inequivalent sublattices allow splitting throughout the Brillouin zone, including at $Γ$. Here, we show that the coplanar noncollinear magnetic state of multiferroic boracite Ni$_3$B$_7$O$_{13}$Cl hosts both motifs on distinct Ni sublattices in real space. The electronic structure and spin texture exhibit coexisting $d$-wave-like and $s$-wave-like spin-polarization components associated with the ALM and CFIM motifs, respectively. Opposite ferroelectric states exhibit reversed band-resolved spin polarizations, indicating magnetoelectric coupling, and sign reversals of linear shift and circular injection currents.

title: Hierarchical universal open structure dataset for atomistic modeling
abstract: Atomic-scale simulations have been transformed by machine-learning models that predict the properties of atomistic structures with the accuracy of quantum calculations, but at a small fraction of the cost. These models have increased dramatically in generality, thanks to the availability of synthetic datasets of ever-increasing size and scope. The proliferation of datasets, with properties often computed using different levels of electronic-structure approximation, is problematic, as there is often overlap between different datasets, and strong correlations between structures obtained with short molecular dynamics trajectories or geometry optimization. To address these problems, we introduce a protocol to stratify a dataset into a hierarchy of nested subsets, subsampling from the coarsest to the finest resolution based on an "ecumetric" built to reflect the latent space representation of several popular universal machine-learning interatomic potentials. We then use this approach to combine most of the open structural datasets currently available, consolidating them into MAD-COSMO, a well-organized collection of almost 1.7 billion structures, whose $2^{24}$ most diverse members form the MAD-CORE stratified coreset, which can be easily used for all sorts of tasks, from exploratory experiments to the training of foundation models at scale. We envision that this collection will guide and help coordinate future efforts, focusing them on the most relevant and/or undersampled regions of chemical and structural space, and that it will be further extended to incorporate the outcomes of the collective work of this community.

title: Scaling up statistical model checking of cyber-physical systems via algorithm ensemble and parallel simulations over HPC infrastructures
abstract: Model-based formal verification of industry-relevant Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) is often a computationally prohibitive task. In most cases, the complexity of the models precludes any prospect of symbolic analysis, leaving numerical simulation as the only viable option. Unfortunately, exhaustive simulation of a CPS model over the entire set of plausible operational scenarios is rarely possible in practice, and alternative strategies such as Statistical Model Checking (SMC) must be used instead. In this article, we show that the number of model simulations (samples) required by SMC techniques to converge can be significantly reduced by considering multiple (an ensemble of) Adaptive Stopping Algorithms (SAs) at once, and that the simulations themselves (by far the most expensive step of the entire workload) can be efficiently sped up by exploiting massively parallel platforms. With three industry-scale CPS models, we experimentally show that the use of an ensemble of two state-of-the-art SAs (AA and EBGStop) may require dozens of millions fewer samples when compared to running a single algorithm, with reductions in sample size of up to 78%. Furthermore, we show that our implementation, by massively parallelizing system model simulations on a HPC infrastructure, yields speed-ups for the completion time of the verification tasks which are practically linear with respect to the number of computational nodes, thus achieving an efficiency of virtually 100%, even on very large platforms. This makes it possible to complete tasks of model-based SMC verification for complex CPSs in a matter of hours or days, whereas a naïve sequential execution would require from months to many years.

title: CF-AVSS: A Coarse-to-Fine Audio-Visual Speech Separation Framework with Target-Speaker Refinement and Post-Fusion for Real-World AVSE Challenge
abstract: Audio-visual speech enhancement (AVSE) leverages visual cues to recover target speech from mixtures corrupted by reverberation, noise, and overlapping speakers. We propose a coarse-to-fine two-stage AVSE framework. In the first stage, a progressive SPAV-TFGridNet is extended to two synchronized visual streams to produce visually ordered coarse estimates by progressively suppressing interfering speech while preserving target reverberation and shared background noise. In the second stage, a TFGridNet-based target speaker refinement network takes the original mixture and both coarse estimates as input to further recover target speech and improve signal quality. The coarse and refined estimates are finally combined using development-set-calibrated fusion. On the ISCSLP 2026 Real-World AVSE Challenge, our system tied for first place on Track 1 and ranked second on Track 2 in OVRL, while achieving the lowest CER on both tracks at 12.31% and 14.79%, respectively.

title: From local chemistry to galactic evolution: unlocking the power of interstellar isotopes with ALMA2040
abstract: Molecular isotopic ratios provide a unique window into the chemical evolution of the interstellar medium, linking stellar nucleosynthesis and Galactic chemical evolution to the physical and chemical processes shaping molecular clouds, star-forming regions, and planetary systems. However, molecular isotopic ratios do not necessarily trace the underlying elemental composition, as chemical isotopic fractionation, isotope-selective photodissociation, grain chemistry, and radiative-transfer effects can significantly alter the observed values. Disentangling these effects requires simultaneous observations of multiple transitions, isotope systems and molecular families, including rare, doubly, and multiply substituted isotopologues involving D, $^{13}$C, $^{15}$N, $^{17,18}$O, $^{29,30}$Si, and $^{33,34,36}$S (e.g., $^{13}$C$^{15}$N, $^{13}$C$^{34}$S, and $^{13}$C$^{18}$O). ALMA2040, with an order-of-magnitude improvement in sensitivity and at least 512 GHz of instantaneous bandwidth, will make these species accessible across statistically significant samples of Galactic and nearby extragalactic sources.
