We evaluate on a renewable variant of the IEEE 118-bus benchmark grid in which 26 of the conventional (synchronous) generators are replaced by inverter-based renewables with battery flexibility and standardised reactive-power limits (IEEE 1547), giving $97\,529$ physically valid (AC-OPF-feasible) operating scenarios, and we ablate all eight combinations of the transfer terms, reporting accuracy against ground truth and fidelity to the teacher separately. Distillation lowers student error on all four predicted quantities, by up to $48\%$ on active-power dispatch, and every distilled student is more accurate than its teacher on reactive-power dispatch. The gain is largely carried by the output matching term. The physics-residual term, in the layer-aggregated form used here, is consistently harmful, which we attribute to the spatial averaging it applies to a bus-level residual field. The resulting student is $32.5\times$ smaller in parameter count and has half the message-passing depth, making it a candidate for subsequent edge-device benchmarking.

title: A general feedback mechanism unifying stochasticity, long transients, and resilience
abstract: Stochasticity in complex systems is commonly treated either as external noise added to deterministic dynamics or as an effective stochastic description of deterministic chaos. A framework in which stochastic dynamics arise endogenously from deterministic chaos and subsequently feed back on the deterministic dynamics, thereby fundamentally reshaping system dynamics, remains rare. Here, we develop such a framework. Through the interaction between deterministic and stochastic dynamics, alternative stable states, critical transitions, adaptive capacity, stochasticity, and resilience become dynamically interconnected within a single model. Furthermore, the framework establishes a new mechanism of long transients, driven by two key factors: (i) time-scale separation and (ii) time-delay-induced cancellation. Stochasticity plays a dual stabilizing-destabilizing role in long transients: it promotes their persistence while also facilitating their eventual escape and collapse. This dual role allows resilience to be quantified dynamically through escape and stochastic recapture dynamics. Finally, we establish the generality of the mechanism mathematically and numerically across a broad class of one-dimensional nonlinear systems, suggesting that it reflects a general dynamical principle.

title: From Action Principle to Stochastic Thermodynamics of Elastic and Viscous Active Matter
abstract: Motivated by the complex material properties of living matter, we derive a framework of stochastic thermo- and elastodynamics for active materials from the classical principle of least action and the Rayleighian formalism for external forces. Our approach couples the local barycentric collective coordinate and the streaming velocity as the canonical conjugate pair, which unifies various descriptions of elastic and viscous soft matter, including Helfrich theory for lipid membranes, linear and nonlinear elasticity of thin shells and deformable droplets, as well as hydrodynamics of active and passive fluids. The Lagrangian mechanics of collective field variables permits direct applications of the results and theorems from statistical mechanics to existing models of complex soft and living matter. To illustrate the potential applications of stochastic elastodynamics in biology, we derive and simulate a boundary-driven deformation model of an elastic cell nucleus in the presence of fluctuations.

title: Contact, Power, and Balls in Play: A Three-Rate Decomposition of Batting Average and the Disappearance of the .400 Hitter
abstract: Batting average factors exactly as BA = c [h + (1-h) b], where c is the rate of avoiding a strikeout, h is the home-run rate among non-strikeout at-bats, and b is batting average on balls in play (BABIP). The bracketed term is the rate f at which non-strikeout at-bats become hits, so the composition nests the two-factor identity BA = c f. Using the 256 major-league hitters with at least 300 at-bats in 2025, every season from 2004 to 2025, and 20,357 qualifying seasons from 1901 to 2019, we ask which rates behave like skills and how the corresponding abilities are related. Over 19 consecutive-season pairs the median year-to-year correlation is 0.86 for c, 0.74 for h and 0.41 for b; batting average (0.44) is no more repeatable than BABIP. A trivariate logistic-normal random-effects model gives single-season reliabilities of 0.91, 0.76 and 0.30, and a talent correlation between contact and power of -0.67 (95% profile interval -0.75 to -0.57), while BABIP talent is only weakly related to either. Historically, the negative covariance between c and f, which was near zero in the dead-ball era, explains why batting averages have become less dispersed, and so why no one has hit .400 since 1941. That covariance runs almost entirely through home runs: removing the contact--power channel from the 2010s covariance recovers 72% of the gap between modern and dead-ball dispersion in batting-average talent.

title: Covariance-Calibrated Prediction-Powered Inference
abstract: Covariance-calibrated prediction-powered inference (CC-PPI) uses unlabeled prediction scores to calibrate the covariance weight in a GMM estimator. The raw target preserves the prediction-corrected channel and replaces the labeled prediction-covariance contribution in the auxiliary residual metric with its unlabeled counterpart. Spectral protection ensures positive definiteness, and the estimator uses an equal blend of the original covariance and the protected target. We establish first-order efficiency and derive exact finite-sample risk identities for linear regression, including a design-based improvement theorem with tolerance to prediction error. A quadratic decision model gives a midpoint minimax-regret interpretation of the half-strength default. Exact strength-path formulas and convergent risk approximations bound its distance from the best fixed strength on that path. Simulations and four real-data studies show substantial reductions in parameter MSE. Independent fixed-strength references yield only small further gains on the calibration paths studied.

title: The space of polarized compactifications of an affine variety
abstract: Let $X$ be a normal affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Through the lens of non-Archimedean geometry, we study the space of polarized compactifications of $X$, consisting of pairs $(\bar X, D)$ where $\bar X$ is a normal projective variety containing $X$ as a dense open subset, and $D$ is an effective ample $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor with support equal to the complement of $X$ in $\bar X$. We identify this space with a natural class of functions--the Fubini--Study functions--on the Berkovich analytification of $X$. Through a Rees correspondence, we also give a bijection with the space of homogeneous $\mathbb{Q}$-valued, finitely generated negative non-Archimedean norms (or filtrations) on the coordinate ring of $X$. Using the above identifications, we equip the space of polarized compactifications, and numerical classes thereof, with natural metrics and identify the metric completions. The latter include a space of continuous plurisubharmonic functions in the sense of Chambert-Loir and Ducros, and a space of birational curve classes as studied by Dang and Favre.

title: Ablation-Driven Selective Laser Direct Mass Transfer for Micro-LEDs with High Speed, Enhanced Gap Tolerance, and High Precision
abstract: Micro light-emitting diodes (micro-LEDs) offer superior performance for next-generation displays, yet their scalable manufacturing is severely bottlenecked by the mass transfer process from donor to receiver substrates. The existing laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT) methods are restricted by low throughput, limited selectivity, and long reaction times. In this study, we introduce a novel defocused direct laser ablation transfer (D-DLAT) method utilizing polyimide as a dynamic release layer. Whereas most indirect laser transfer methods trigger chip release followed by passive descent toward the receiver, D-DLAT directly ablates the release layer to actively propel the small-sized chips towards the receiver via ablation shock. By optimizing the ablation profiles and scanning paths, this method achieves high-speed transfer with significantly enhanced precision and robustness. We demonstrate the successful transfer of micro-LEDs ranging from 600 $\unicode{x03BC}$m down to 35 $\unicode{x03BC}$m in size, with a minimum reported placement error of less than 1 $\unicode{x03BC}$m, and a critical transfer gap of up to 50 $\unicode{x03BC}$m. Furthermore, the D-DLAT approach enables full selectivity, facilitating complex patterned transfers and array repitching operations that are essential for full-color display integration. Our findings indicate that D-DLAT effectively overcomes the fundamental limitations of current transfer technologies, demonstrating substantial potential for the scalable and high-yield manufacturing of advanced micro-LED displays. Ultimately, D-DLAT establishes a robust paradigm for the high-speed manipulation and heterogeneous integration of micro-optoelectronic devices, extending its profound implications beyond displays to the broader landscape of advanced micro-assembly and flexible electronics.

title: Surjective maps preserving quasi-nilpotence of products of operators
abstract: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space and let $\mathcal B(X)$ the full algebra of all bounded linear operator on $X$. In this paper, we give a complete characterization of surjective maps $ϕ:\mathcal B(X)\to\mathcal B(X)$ satisfying \[ r(AB)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r(ϕ(A)ϕ(B))=0 \qquad(A,B\in\mathcal B(X)). \] Without assuming additivity, injectivity, or continuity, we show that there exists a function $γ: B(X)\mapsto \C \setminus\{0\}$ such that the map $ϕ$ takes one of the following forms: 1. there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X\to X$ such that : \label{eq:direct} ϕ(A)=γ(A)SAS^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X), 2. the space $X$ is reflexive and there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X^*\to X$ such that \label{eq:dual} ϕ(A)=γ(A)SA^*S^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X).

title: Feeling the generalised rough SABR boundary
abstract: We provide an in-depth analysis of a generalised rough version of the SABR volatility model, widely used in the financial industry. We specifically focus on its behaviour at the origin, whether it can reach it and how fast it may do so.

title: Synchronization induced by stochastic subsystem resetting in complex networks
abstract: We study synchronization in network-coupled oscillators subject to stochastic resetting of a subset of nodes. We show that resetting can induce collective coherence in oscillators that are never directly reset, through the interplay of network structure, frequency heterogeneity, and the organization of the reset subsystem. In the infinite-resetting-rate limit, the reset nodes become effectively pinned to a reference phase, and linearization near synchronization maps the dynamics of the remaining subsystem onto a grounded-Laplacian problem. This formulation yields an analytical relation between the synchronization level and the reset parameters, providing an estimate of the coupling strength required to achieve a prescribed degree of coherence. Beyond the linear regime, we develop a mean-field description in which the reset subsystem acts as an effective ordering field for the remaining oscillators. Numerical simulations across different network topologies confirm these predictions and show that synchronization is enhanced by increasing both the reset fraction and network connectivity. In heterogeneous networks, the placement of reset nodes can strongly influence the synchronization response. For frequency distributions with nonzero mean, resetting competes with the intrinsic collective rotation and can drive the system from a rotating synchronized state to a phase-locked state. These results establish subsystem resetting as a mechanism for inducing and controlling collective synchronization in complex networks.

title: Series and Parallel Dependency Links: Vitality for Interdependent Networks of Networks
abstract: In a network of networks, a dependency link runs from a supplier to the node it serves and binds the supplier's failure to the node's failure. Indices computed from the graph topology leave aside the service each edge carries, but in real interdependent systems that service decides how failure propagates: a pumping station requires electricity and telemetry, and losing either stops it; a district fed by either of two reservoirs survives the loss of one. Building on this observation, we label each node of the network with the service it provides. We then measure how far this qualitative input can change the node's vitality ranking: by fixing the graph topology we show that changing only the labels moves the Mean Operativity Loss from $0.023$ to $0.114$, while a ranking computed from the unlabelled graph topology is blind to the difference. The links give a node its suppliers; the labels group those suppliers into alternatives within one service and joint requirements across services. These labels should belong to the description of an interdependent system alongside the links themselves for a fidelity vitality measure

title: Secular Evolution of Quasiperiodic Eruptions: eRO-QPE2
abstract: Quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) are recurrent soft X-ray flares from galactic nuclei. In this work, we analyze both the quiescent and eruption emission of eRO-QPE2, using 11 XMM-Newton observations spanning $4.33\,{\rm yr}$. The key findings include (1) the eruption peak count rate remains approximately constant, while the quiescent count rate shows an approximately linear decline superposed with a large-amplitude oscillation; (2) no secondary eruptions are detected between the normal eruptions and any such events would have to be fainter by more than two orders of magnitude; (3) the recurrence time decreases at an average rate of $\dot{T}_{\rm rec}\approx-5\times10^{-6}$. These findings are consistent with an extreme mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) interacting with a precessing accretion disk and producing two normal eruptions per orbital period. Bayesian timing analyses further constrain the EMRI orbital eccentricity to $e<0.033$ (at $95\%$ confidence level).

title: Temporal Periodic Image Registration with Implicit Neural Representations
abstract: Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) have recently gained popularity for their ability to model functions using simple and lightweight networks. These methods have also proven effective in deformable image registration. In this work, we extend INRs for deformable image registration to the domain of temporal image registration, focusing on periodic temporal image sequences. Our approach, Temporal-IDIR, optimizes a single INR to model deformations across all frames in a temporal image sequence simultaneously, allowing for self-regularization through its own deformation predictions. To achieve this, we introduce a temporal consistency loss that penalizes discrepancies between direct source-to-target transformations and those traversing intermediate frames. We evaluate our framework on the DIR-LAB dataset, using the target registration error (TRE) between annotated and moved landmarks as the metric. Here, we achieve a TRE of 1.03 mm, outperforming other INR-based registration methods. Additionally, our framework supports smooth interpolation between time frames by estimating deformations between the given input frames. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/MMLowes/Temporal_INR.

title: Where Backtests and Live Trading Part Ways: Six Defects from One Intraday System
abstract: Backtests of intraday strategies can drift away from what the live system actually does; in our case, the drift never showed in summary statistics. We report six defects found while running one intraday US equity system live and comparing its live days with their backtest replay. Three came from data: a default feed that carried a small fraction of real opening volume, historical prices adjusted for dividends that live orders never see, and data the live system downloaded but the backtest never did. Two came from code: a sizing step that exceeded a limit the live account enforces, and UTC timestamps read as New York time. One came from configuration: settings that were switched on but never reached the code that places orders. For each we give the symptom, the size of the error, the cause and the test or control that now guards against it. All six sat where two paths that should agree had drifted apart. We close with a ten-point checklist. We make no claim about whether the system is profitable.

title: A geometry-independent endpoint estimate for the Littlewood--Paley $g$-function generated by the Poisson semigroup
abstract: We prove a weak $(1,1)$ estimate for the full Poisson Littlewood--Paley $g$-function on every complete Riemannian manifold without boundary, with an explicit universal constant approximately equal to $3.33606$. The estimate requires no curvature restriction, volume doubling, heat kernel bound, or stochastic completeness. The proof combines a precise Poisson maximal inequality with a convex entropy identity; local elliptic regularity identifies the extension to arbitrary real $L^1$ data. As an application, we obtain weak $(1,1)$ estimates for certain spectral multipliers represented by Poisson time derivatives with coefficients in $L^2((0,\infty),dt/t)$.

title: Photon-Return and Polar-Focusing Crossovers near Extremal Kerr
abstract: How precisely must a photon's impact parameter be tuned for it to complete $n$ windings around a nearly extremal Kerr black hole before escaping, and how does the same near extremal scaling control the focusing of neighboring rays? For equatorial prograde returns we find, with $κ=\sqrt{1-a^2/M^2}$ and $X=nκ$, $ε_n=\sqrt{3}\,κ/(e^{2πX}-1) +O(κ^2|\lnκ|)$. This single law connects the extremal inverse-winding hierarchy to subextremal exponential accumulation. Perturbing the return family quasi-equatorially, we derive a second scaling law for the polar Jacobi phase, $Ψ_θ=2\ln[\sinh(πX)/κ]+C_s+o(1)$, and show that its focusing points cross from geometric spacing in winding number to asymptotically uniform spacing $Δ\mathcal N\simeq(2κ)^{-1}$. Numerical integrations of the exact Kerr radial dynamics and linear polar equation verify both scaling collapses. Thus near extremal Kerr exhibits parametrically distinct winding and polar-focusing scales, rather than a discontinuous jump between extremal and subextremal lensing hierarchies.

title: Frontiers of chemical complexity in the interstellar medium: unveiling the cosmic origins of life
abstract: The interstellar medium (ISM) contains a rich molecular inventory that provides a unique window into the chemistry operating during star and planet formation and its connection to prebiotic chemistry. More than 350 interstellar molecules are currently known, including increasingly complex organic molecules and species containing elements beyond the second row of the periodic table. Yet the limits that interstellar chemical complexity can reach, its evolution from molecular clouds to planetary systems, and its contribution to the molecular feedstock of life remain poorly constrained. Addressing these questions requires sensitive, broadband observations capable of detecting multiple weak rotational transitions of molecular species, such as amino acids, nucleobases, sugars and lipids, towards star- and planet-forming environments. Current facilities, including ALMA, are limited by instantaneous spectral coverage, sensitivity (especially on extended spatial scales), and the trade-off between total bandwidth and integration time. The proposed ALMA2040 facility would overcome these limitations through at least a tenfold improvement in spectral-line sensitivity, high-fidelity imaging from sub-arcsecond to tens-of-arcsecond scales, and ultra-broad instantaneous frequency coverage from 35 to 950 GHz at high spectral resolution. These capabilities would allow systematic detections of species with molecular abundances with respect to H$_2$ below 10$^{-11}$, facilitating the identification of new complex and heavy-element-bearing species through multiple transitions, and providing complete molecular inventories across evolutionary stages. ALMA2040 would thus make it possible to comprehensively investigate the emergence and evolution of chemical complexity, and to determine whether molecular precursors of prebiotic chemistry are widespread throughout the Galaxy.

title: Seeing Both the Forest and the Trees: Reusing Holistic 3D Priors for Part-Decomposed Generation
abstract: Generating 3D assets with explicit parts requires two properties at once: geometric detail inside each part and structural coherence across the whole object. Recent image-conditioned 3D generation models adopt a structured 3D representation that anchors tokens to explicit spatial positions, capturing both properties, but their output remains a single fused mesh. We ask how a part-decomposed generation model can inherit both properties of these holistic priors, and answer with STRUCTPARTS, a framework whose core technical contribution is a dual-frame coordinate interleaving mechanism: each shape latent is interpreted under both a part-local and an object-global reference frame, and processed through a global-local inter-leaved transformer that simultaneously reuses the prior's geometric detail at the part scale and its structural coherence at the whole-object scale. As its structural input, STRUCTPARTS uses a segmented mesh scaffold, a coarse mesh paired with a face-level segmentation mask kept entirely within the prior's native 3D representation. With only lightweight finetuning, both intra-part detail and inter-part coherence emerge from the same pretrained weights. On PartObjaverse-Tiny, STRUCTPARTS matches or surpasses prior part-decomposed models at a fraction of their training cost, while naturally supporting part-mesh refinement and part-level editing.

title: Evolved stars: dust formation and mass loss
abstract: Evolved stars drive the chemical enrichment of the Universe, acting as primary producers of elemental products of nucleosynthesis and cosmic dust. Unraveling the exact role played by these objects requires empirical constraints on the interplay between pulsation, convection, magnetic fields, mass loss, and dust formation at small (milliarcsecond) scales, currently limited to only a handful of sources. Next-generation facilities, particularly the new ALMA2040, will enable systematic, spatially resolved studies of mass loss and dust formation across large samples of evolved stars, expanding from a few tens to hundreds of objects and providing the empirical constraints needed to understand the recycling and chemical enrichment of baryonic matter throughout the Universe.

title: MAGMA: Multiplier-Augmented Geometric Motion Algorithm
abstract: Solving optimal control problems for high-dimensional mechanical systems subject to constraints remains challenging due to nonlinear dynamics and non-convex feasible sets. This paper introduces MAGMA(Multiplier-Augmented Geometric Motion Algorithm), an Affine Geometric Heat Flow (AGHF)-based trajectory optimizer that incorporates an augmented Lagrangian framework solved via a primal-dual flow. A theoretical characterization of the primal-dual AGHF is provided, establishing that MAGMA is a gradient flow on an appropriately defined energy. MAGMA is validated across a variety of challenging trajectory generation problems with obstacles, state limits, and actuation limits. Comparative evaluations against state-of-the-art solvers demonstrate that MAGMA achieves high quality solutions with significantly reduced tuning effort on the hardest problems.

title: Superconducting circuits host two-level systems with lifetimes exceeding one second
abstract: Understanding the microscopic environment of superconducting qubits is a central challenge for quantum technologies. Parasitic two-level systems (TLSs) of various microscopic origins are ubiquitous and limit qubit performance through decoherence, frequency drifts, and leakage. Recently, long-lived TLSs with lifetimes exceeding those of state-of-the-art qubits have been shown to induce correlated qubit dynamics, with direct implications for quantum error correction. Here, we perform wide-band quantum-jump correlation spectroscopy on flux-tunable transmon qubits and identify microscopic degrees of freedom that outlive the qubit by orders of magnitude. Pump-probe measurements at varying detunings from these objects reveal intrinsic lifetimes exceeding one second. Their weak coupling to the qubit, in the kilohertz range, is consistent with positional defects described by the standard tunneling model, without excluding other microscopic origins such as magnetic spin impurities or trapped quasiparticles. More broadly, these results establish superconducting qubits as a sensitive probe of exceptionally long-lived microscopic degrees of freedom and open a route toward their controlled access and functionalization.

title: Interlocked Vortex Order in the Frustrated $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ Lattice ($A$=Cs,Rb)
abstract: Recently synthesized $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ ($A$ = Cs, Rb) provides a unique platform for exploring the interplay between geometric frustration, magnetism, and correlated electronic states beyond conventional kagome systems. Based on first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that the frustrated V sublattice naturally stabilizes a robust vortex or anti-vortex antiferromagnetic ground state, whose total energy is substantially lower than all other configurations. In addition, the Heisenberg model analysis show strong constraints on the ground state magnetic configuration, such that fixing spin configuration of 1 triangle propagates and fixes all others. The vortex or anti-vortex phase hosts electronic structures reminiscent of kagome metals, including Dirac-like band crossings, van Hove singularities, and flat bands near the Fermi level. Owing to the noncollinear spin texture and quasi-two-dimensional magnetic character, the Néel temperature exhibits an extremely weak dependence on both the magnitude and direction of external magnetic fields, consistent with experimental observations. For Cs-based compound, the ground state band structure is metallic with 6 Weyl points in the BZ; while for the Rb-based compound, spin--orbit coupling opens an approximately 27-meV gap at ambient pressure due to the lifted C$_3$ symmetry. Our results establish $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ as a promising platform for studying frustration-driven chiral magnetism and its interplay with topological electronic states.

title: The Calderón operator for time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in closed waveguides
abstract: We consider the time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in a closed, cylindrical waveguide with longitudinal invariant but heterogeneous permittivity and permeability. We consider minimal smoothness assumptions, i.e., the material parameters have to be in $L^\infty$ and the cross section has to be Lipschitz with a possibly non-trivial topology. First, we show that the associated Calderón operator is well-defined and bounded in the natural trace spaces $\mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_Γ;Γ) \to \mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{div}_Γ;Γ)$. Second, we consider interior Maxwell problems obtained from using the Calderón operator and analyze their well-posedness. Furthermore, we report some additional results on the location and group velocities of the waveguide wavenumbers.

title: Large in-plane optical anisotropy in epitaxial CrN(113) films
abstract: CrN, a transition-metal nitride crystallizing in the cubic rocksalt structure, exhibits a unique combination of mechanical robustness, semiconducting behavior, and thermoelectric functionality. To date, however, CrN has been synthesized primarily as polycrystalline material or as epitaxial films grown along high-symmetry orientations such as (001) and (111). Here, we prepare epitaxial CrN(113) films on AlN(11\bar{2}2) templates by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. The low-symmetry interface and highly direction dependent lattice mismatch are expected to modify the physical properties of CrN relative to the bulk material. Indeed, variable-angle spectroscopic ellipsometry in the photon-energy range from 1.25 to 5 eV reveals a surprisingly strong polarization dependence of the optical response despite the nearly strain-free cubic crystal structure of the films. The pseudo-optical constants n and k differ by more than 10% for orthogonal in-plane polarizations throughout the investigated spectral range. We evaluate possible origins of this effect and conclude that it most likely arises from anisotropic surface morphology of CrN(113), which creates a metasurface acting as a subwavelength grating in the strongly absorbing regime.

title: High-order positivity-preserving well-balanced schemes: combining flux globalization with modified Patankar deferred correction methods
abstract: Positivity-preserving schemes for hyperbolic balance laws are typically built from the Zhang-Shu limiter and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta (SSP-RK) time stepping, at the cost of a restrictive time-step condition. The modified Patankar deferred correction (mPDeC) method removes this restriction, offering high-order accuracy, conservation, and unconditional positivity. However, its solution-dependent Patankar weights make the time update nonlinear, so, unlike with RK methods, preserving (steady and moving) equilibria, i.e., well-balancing (WB), is no longer straightforward. In this paper, we construct high-order, WB, positivity-preserving mPDeC schemes by combining mPDeC with a flux-globalization approach. We demonstrate the idea on the one-dimensional shallow water equations, using a WB A-WENO spatial discretization, and introduce a modified local characteristic decomposition that remains stable in the presence of dry states. Numerical experiments on one-dimensional benchmarks confirm that the method satisfies the desired properties.

title: Multiplex coupling: Connecting the intellectual base and the topics of a research field
abstract: Two documents can be close because they cite the same works or because they write about the same things, and the two kinds of proximity often disagree. Science mapping reads them in separate maps or merges them, as hybrid clustering does; either way the disagreement is lost. We introduce multiplex coupling, a framework that couples the same documents by their references and by their terms, keeps the two layers separate and analyses their relation. Similarities are standardised against a null model, and the agreement between the layers is measured on random pairs of documents. Consensus clustering partitions each layer into roots, groups sharing an intellectual base, and themes, groups sharing a topic. A test on the roots $\times$ themes table identifies branching roots and convergent themes, and pairs of roots are followed over time. Every structure is reported with its persistence across numbers of neighbours, which on synthetic data identifies most false branching. Applications to Web of Science, Scopus and OpenAlex collections show that the two layers carry largely complementary information, and reveal substantive and methodological bases that have grown into several topics. The framework is implemented in bibliometrix.

title: Weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}$-object
abstract: $\mathbb{P}$-objects were introduced by Huybrechts and Thomas as a generalization of spherical objects. We classify the weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object in the sense of Krug. For $n=1$, this recovers the classification of weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a spherical object due to Holm, Jorgensen and Yang. We also compute the Koszul-dual model of the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object.

title: From Accelerating Rotating Black Holes to a Swirling Universe
abstract: We demonstrate that the swirling universe can be recovered through a coordinated horizon-degeneration and scaling procedure applied to the Kerr C-metric. The construction exploits the horizon structure of accelerating, rotating black holes, which allows their inner and outer horizons to coalesce while simultaneously approaching the acceleration horizon. By magnifying the near-acceleration-horizon region faster than the black hole horizons approach it, the pair of accelerating, rotating black holes is pushed to an infinite proper distance, while a finite gravitomagnetic twist survives. The resulting geometry reproduces precisely the swirling universe, providing a physical interpretation of its intrinsic rotation as the gravitational remnant of rotating black holes sent to infinity.

title: Diffusion-Induced Stabilization of Nonreciprocal Wealth Dynamics
abstract: We study the stability of equal wealth shares in a spatial model combining local sharing, global redistribution, and random nonreciprocal interactions. On a two-dimensional square lattice in the infinite-system limit, the effect of local sharing depends on whether the influence of one site on another tends to have the same or opposite sign as the reverse influence. When these influences are nonnegatively correlated, diffusion reduces the redistribution required for stability, but a positive rate remains necessary. Negative correlations instead allow stability without redistribution, with the largest stability margin at finite diffusion and a return toward marginal stability at strong diffusion. This nonmonotonicity reflects a competition between spatial smoothing and the weakening of the stabilizing contribution of reciprocal anticorrelations. Equal shares can even remain stable under wealth-concentrating transfers, but only within an intermediate range of diffusion strengths.

title: Dynamic ordering in sequence generation in Transformers: experiments on low-resource Tagging scenarios
abstract: This paper introduces TagInsert, a Transformer-based model that challenges the common left-to-right (L2R) generation paradigm in Transformers, for sequence labelling tasks where dependencies may not naturally align with a L2R order. TagInsert lifts the L2R constraint by removing the decoder-side attention mask and enabling the model to decide a preferred order of tag generation at inference time. We experiment on the common Part-of-Speech tagging and the more complex Combinatory Categorial Grammar (CCG) supertagging tasks on multiple languages and low-resource data settings. We show that, although encoder-only models like BERT remain strong performers for tagging tasks, TagInsert frequently outperforms a L2R encoder-decoder model, achieves results comparable to encoder-only models under data-scarce conditions, and shows better results on the long-tail of rare categories. Our analyses show that TagInsert alleviates error propagation typical of autoregressive models by learning to defer difficult predictions to later stages in the decoding process.

title: Convective Oscillations of Cosmic Rays
abstract: Turbulent motion of the background plasma can introduce fluctuations in the spatial distribution of cosmic rays (CRs). For an ensemble-averaged Gaussian CR distribution with a width $ Λ\left( t,p \right) $ at time $ t $ and momentum $ p $, it is found that $ P_\text{s}\left( t,k,p \right) $ and $ P_\text{d}\left( t,k,p \right) $, the fluctuation power spectra induced by incompressible and acoustic turbulent convection, respectively, have power-law asymptotics in wavenumber $ k $: $ P_\text{s}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^4 $ and $ P_\text{d}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^2 $ for $ k\ll 1/Λ\left( t,p \right) $; $ P_\text{s}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^{γ_\text{s}-4} $ for $ k\gg 1/L_\text{s} $, and $ P_\text{d}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^{γ_\text{d}-2} $ for $ k\gg 1/L_\text{d} $, where $ γ_\text{s} $ and $ γ_\text{d} $ are the spectral indices of the velocity power spectra of the incompressible and acoustic turbulence below their outer scales $ L_\text{s} $ and $ L_\text{d} $, respectively. These results have implications for probing interstellar turbulence via future high-resolution images of pulsar gamma-ray halos.

title: Localisation of the monkey walk with an "impurity" at the origin
abstract: The monkey walk is a model of reinforced random walk introduced by Boyer and Solis-Salas as a model for the exploratory behaviour of capuchin monkeys. At each step of the walk, the walker flips a biased coin to determine whether to take a simple, symmetric random walk step on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ or to "relocate", i.e. choose a time uniformly at random in its past and jump to where it was at that time. More recently, Boyer, Falcón-Cortés, Giuggioli and Majumdar looked at a modification of the model, where the probability to relocate is $ξ_0$ when the walker sits at the origin and $ξ>ξ_0$ anywhere else. We prove that, for all $ξ_0\in (0,1)$, if $ξ$ is sufficiently close to 1, then the monkey walk "localises", i.e. the position of the walker at time $n$, $W_n$, converges in distribution without any renormalisation. (We in fact prove convergence of the occupation measure of the walker.) This is in contrast with the case when $ξ= ξ_0$, for which it is known that $W_n/\sqrt{\log n}$ converges in distribution to a standard Gaussian (we say that the walk "diffuses"). Our proof relies on seeing the monkey walk as an infinitely-many colour Pólya urn (a.k.a. measure-valued Pólya process - MVPP) and then prove convergence of this urn, which is not straightforward as theorems from the literature on MVPPs do not apply directly.

title: From Sketch to Scene: Relightable Garment Reconstruction from Marked Sketches
abstract: Sketching is one of the most natural ways for people to express visual ideas. Unlike the text prompts that most generative systems rely on today, a sketch captures spatial structure and intent directly, including where a designer wants highlights and shadows to appear. Yet current sketch-to-3D pipelines have no input for that intent: they bake the drawn shading into the texture as dark paint, and the light cannot be moved. We propose a system that transforms a rough garment sketch, marked with sparse annotations (a star for a highlight and a moon for a shadow), and a short text prompt describing the texture, into a textured 3D mesh with an explicit directional light, as a scene that can be relit and edited after generation. The two symbols are the most frequent proposals in an elicitation study with art students. From the marked sketch the system predicts the scene's directional light and, separately, a displacement field that bends the surface so that the moon-marked regions fall into shadow under that light, rather than being painted dark in the texture.

title: Edge ideals of gapfree graphs with matching number $3$
abstract: We prove that if $G$ is a gapfree graph with matching number $3$, then every power $I(G)^q$, $q\geq2$, of its edge ideal has linear quotients, and hence a linear resolution. Our approach combines graph reductions based on clique domination of gapfree graphs and matching number with operations preserving linear quotients. We reduce the problem to $26$ non-co-chordal graphs on at most seven vertices. A new preservation theorem for gapfree edge addition, together with known results on duplication and gapfree expansion, handles all but one of these graphs. For the remaining graph on seven vertices, we construct a linear quotients ordering for the square and extend it recursively to every higher power.

title: Algorithmic Collusion Without Deterrence: Auditing the Punishment Mechanism in Q-Learning Pricing Agents
abstract: Independent tabular Q-learning agents repricing in a simulated Bertrand duopoly converge to supracompetitive prices, and the seminal evidence attributes this to a learned reward-punishment scheme: undercut your rival and it retaliates, so deviation never pays. This mechanistic reading is what turns high prices into a cartel, and into a regulatory target. We replicate the environment of Calvano et al. (2020) and confirm their impulse-response pattern within co-trained pairs. We then audit the pattern on frozen policies, with learning off, and find that on its own it does not identify a mechanism: the return is over-determined rather than selective. In nine of ten converged pairs (914 of 1,024) a single attractor's basin is the entire state space, so every perturbation returns whatever provoked it, and a forced price increase triggers the same retaliatory pattern as an undercut. What co-training produces is a narrow, dyad-specific basin of attraction: re-match frozen agents from independent runs, as Calvano et al. did with learning on, and coordination collapses by 80% with nothing carried across. The deterrence claim is incomplete on its own terms: the one-period undercut of Calvano et al.'s impulse-response test is unprofitable, which we confirm in 92% of pairs, but the optimal deviation, computed by dynamic programming against each partner's frozen strategy, profits by 17.5% on average. The scheme deters only the deviation no optimizer would choose; collusion survives because deviation is never tried, not because it would not pay. Supracompetitive prices are robust; the punishment mechanism read into them does not survive these tests, which changes what the standard test of algorithmic collusion establishes, and what pairing-disruption remedies can be expected to do.

title: Rich-neighbor 5-edge-colorings of subcubic graphs whose 3-vertices induce a matching
abstract: Let $φ$ be a proper edge-coloring of a graph $G$. An edge is called rich if all edges adjacent to it receive pairwise distinct colors. The coloring $φ$ is a rich-neighbor edge-coloring if every non-isolated edge is adjacent to a rich edge. Petruševski and Škrekovski introduced this notion as a relaxation of strong edge-coloring and conjectured that every connected subcubic graph other than $K_4$ admits a rich-neighbor $5$-edge-coloring. We establish the conjectured bound for every subcubic graph $G$ satisfying $Δ(G[V_3])\leq 1,$ where $V_3$ is the set of vertices of degree $3$ in $G$. Equivalently, the $3$-vertices of $G$ induce a matching together with isolated vertices. This extends the result of Chen, Tan and Zhou for subcubic graphs with no adjacent $3$-vertices.

title: Lethe: Link Inference Attacks For Evaluation of Edge Unlearning Methods
abstract: Graph Unlearning (GU) aims to remove the influence of specific training data from a Graph Neural Network without retraining anew. While most methods address removal of nodes and features, Edge Unlearning (EU), aiming at forgetting edges, has recently attracted dedicated attention as a standalone problem due to the hardness of completely removing the impact of an edge in the model. Despite this, no dedicated benchmark for EU exists besides isolated evaluations on feature-rich datasets such as Cora and Citeseer where GNNs exploit node features rather than graph structure. As such, we show two systematic limitations in existing evaluations: dedicated EU methods can be slower than retraining anew, and accuracy metrics are uninformative due to the negligible impact of edge removal. To address this gap, we introduce Lethe, the first comprehensive benchmark for Edge Unlearning, featuring 15 methods and 8 datasets. Our benchmark emphasizes large graphs, introduces evaluation tasks of varying difficulty, and proposes empirical measures based on link inference attacks rather than proxy accuracy metrics. We provide a comprehensive empirical analysis, demonstrate the shortcomings of current evaluations, and release Lethe as a reproducible, extensible benchmark.

title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents
abstract: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) addresses decision-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes. Learning risk-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly. Existing work on risk-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent (OCE), a general class of risk measures. We consider two formulations: dynamic-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem's fundamental limits. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least-squares value-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation. We establish utility-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic- and static-OCE RL.

title: Twisted Artin-Schreier Theory I: $(C_p \rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of local function fields
abstract: Over any field $K$ of characteristic $p$, we parametrize the $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ using pairs of elements $(g,a) \in K\times K^\times$, via a "twisted" variant of Artin-Schreier theory. Focusing on the case of the local function field $K := \mathbb F_q(\!(π)\!)$ over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ of characteristic $p$, we use this parametrization to obtain an exact formula for the count of all $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ with a given discriminant.

title: On Minimum Divergence for Distribution Reconstruction
abstract: We study the possibility of generalizing maximum-entropy reconstruction, which approximately recovers a probability distribution from finitely many (generalized) moments by minimizing the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence to a reference measure. The reconstruction lies in an exponential family and is also the best KL approximation of the unknown distribution within that family: moment matching and information projection coincide. Replacing KL by a smooth f-divergence, the reconstruction still exists in an associated family, but the best approximation property does not. Specifically, a family is called entropy-adapted if the projection of any distribution matches its moments. We show that, up to equivalence, KL is the only $C^2$ f-divergence that is entropy-adapted, whatever the choice of the generalized moments. We illustrate the consequences of this failure numerically.

title: Volterra operators on the BMOA space of Dirichlet series
abstract: In this paper, we completely characterize the boundedness and compactness of Volterra operators on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\), the BMOA space of Dirichlet series, and estimate their essential and weak essential norms. We further prove that compactness, weak compactness, and complete continuity are equivalent for these operators. In particular, every Dirichlet polynomial symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\). We also prove that every such symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on the Bergman space of Dirichlet series \(\mathcal A_μ^1\) for every admissible measure \(μ\), extending the corresponding compactness theorem, previously established for \(1<p<\infty\), to the endpoint \(p=1\).

title: Strong NP-Hardness of Rank-2 Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
abstract: Nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) approximates a nonnegative matrix by the product of two nonnegative matrices with a prescribed inner dimension~$r$. The existence of an exact NMF can be decided in polynomial time for every fixed~$r$, and a best rank-$1$ NMF in the Frobenius norm can be obtained from a truncated singular value decomposition. We prove that computing a best rank-$2$ NMF in the Frobenius norm is strongly NP-hard. Our proof uses a polynomial-time reduction from \textsc{Clique} that produces symmetric positive-definite, completely positive matrices with polynomially bounded integer entries. The same reduction also establishes strong NP-hardness of rank-$2$ symmetric NMF.

title: Microwave spectroscopic evidence of a moiré-commensurate electron crystal in monolayer graphene
abstract: We probe the conductivity of the lowest Landau level of a moiré-aligned monolayer graphene device by broadband microwave transmission through a coplanar waveguide ($\sim$50 mK, 15.4--18 T), isolating the longitudinal channel through a low-minus-high frequency band difference $D(ν)$. We resolve a series of minima in $D(ν)$ that drift with field along lines of fixed carrier density rather than fixed Landau filling, the hallmark of moiré-commensurate electron crystals. The strongest minimum is present at every field and matches no fractional quantum Hall or integer Hofstadter state. It lies at band filling $s=1/3$, one electron for every three moiré cells---the generalized Wigner crystal that DaSilva, Jung, and MacDonald predict as the most favorable fixed-density ($t=0$) commensuration. The weaker minima fall near neighboring commensurate fillings.

title: Optical Coherent Combining in Multi-Aperture Free-Space Receivers through Atmospheric Turbulence via Optically Computed Alignment Gradients
abstract: Multi-aperture reception converts spatial diversity into a coherent-combining gain, but only if the relative phase and polarization of the collected field replicas are aligned before they are summed. In a satellite-to-ground downlink the atmosphere perturbs amplitude, phase and polarization, so the alignment must track a fluctuating channel rather than a fixed offset. This paper proposes a new optical-domain combining scheme in which the alignment information is computed by light itself: the ascent directions that maximize the combined output power are formed by optical interference and read out directly as differential photocurrents of balanced detection, so no estimate of the channel, no deliberate perturbation, and no per-branch digital processing is needed to obtain them. Every branch is aligned against one shared reference - a passive tap of the combined field itself - so no independent laser or optical frequency lock is required, and the update directions of all branches are available simultaneously in a single averaging window without frequency, code, or time multiplexing. The data path needs a single dual-polarization coherent receiver regardless of the aperture count, and the readout is built from elementary parts only - a 3 dB directional coupler, static phase shifters, a Faraday rotator, and balanced photodiodes - so no 90-degree optical hybrid, mixer, or polarization-diverse hybrid is required. The phase and polarization loops are fixed-gain and division-free, and each branch carries one phase modulator and one polarization controller with no amplitude actuator. A closed-form combining-gain and loss budget is derived, the assumptions and limitations of the scheme are stated explicitly, and experimental validation remains open.

title: Aligning LLMs with Sparse Retrieval via Adaptive Sparse Supervision
abstract: While large language models (LLMs) offer strong semantic representations, their application to first-stage retrieval incurs substantial latency and storage costs. Neural sparse retrievers such as SPLADE provide efficient retrieval but rely on relatively compact encoders with limited representational capacity. To bridge this gap, we propose an LLM-based sparse retrieval framework with input-adaptive sparse alignment. Specifically, we introduce a dynamic $α$-truncation strategy that selects input-specific supervision supports based on the cumulative activation mass of SPLADE representations. This strategy guides the LLM to preserve salient lexical signals while suppressing less informative activations, without relying on a fixed support budget. Subsequent retrieval fine-tuning combines contrastive learning, knowledge distillation, and sparsity regularization to improve retrieval effectiveness. Experiments on MS MARCO and six selected BEIR datasets demonstrate improvements over SPLADE++ while maintaining competitive effectiveness against LLM-based sparse retrievers. Compared with Lion-sp, our method reduces index storage by 6.4-fold and end-to-end query latency by over 11-fold, achieving a favorable effectiveness-efficiency trade-off.

title: A Linear-Time Algorithm for the Unbiased Claw Game on Graphs with Maximum Degree 4
abstract: We study the unbiased Maker-Breaker $K_{1,3}$-game, the unbiased claw game, played on the edge set of a general graph $G$. In this game, Maker and Breaker alternatingly claim edges of $G$, and Maker wins if his claimed edges contain a claw once no more edges are available. Graphs with maximum degree at least 5 are Maker's win. A graph $G$ is claw-connected if the hypergraph modeling the unbiased claw game played on $G$ is connected. We characterize Maker's win in the unbiased claw game on every claw-connected graph whose maximum degree is different from 3. Our main structural result is a complete characterization of Maker's win for claw-connected graphs with exactly one vertex of degree 4. The analysis is based on the fact that vertices of degree 4 act as forcing structures. Our characterization results in a linear-time algorithm for the unbiased claw game on claw-connected graphs with maximum degree different from 3. We also obtain a linear-time decomposition algorithm reducing the game on general graphs to a collection of pairwise edge-disjoint claw-connected subgraphs of maximum degree exactly 3, thereby isolating the only remaining case. This decomposition yields an $\mathcal{O}(|V(G)|^3)$-time algorithm for the unbiased claw game on general graphs, improving on the $\mathcal{O}(|V(G)|^7)$-time algorithm implied by the work of Galliot, Gravier and Sivignon (arXiv 2026). For a lower bound on the decision complexity, we prove that any agent deciding the game in the adjacency-array model makes at least $Ω(|V(G)|)$ queries in the worst case, indicating the optimality of our linear-time algorithm.

title: One generation of the Standard Model as a quantum error-correcting code
abstract: Together with a right-handed neutrino, the fermions of one generation of the Standard Model are labelled by five bits, a combinatorial structure tied to anomaly cancellation. We make this precise. Anomaly cancellation is the vanishing of a cubic form, the defining property of triorthogonal codes, the quantum error-correcting codes behind magic state distillation. Removing the right-handed neutrino gives a $[[15,1,3]]_p$ code for every prime $p$, including the Bravyi-Kitaev code for $p = 2$. For qutrits it is the unique shortest distance-three triorthogonal code.

title: Confidence-Guided Adaptive Beam Selection for Vision-Aided Beam Tracking in mmWave Systems
abstract: Vision-aided beam tracking reduces mmWave beam-training overhead by predicting beam indices from camera observations. Fixed top-$K$ selection, however, assigns the same candidate beam budget to all predictions, ignoring uncertainty variations across samples and horizons. This letter proposes confidence-guided adaptive candidate selection: predictor logits are temperature-calibrated, and the smallest top-ranked beam set whose cumulative probability reaches a target threshold is retained under a maximum budget. On DeepSense~6G Scenario~8, over five random seeds and at matched overhead, the policy improves candidate set accuracy by up to 3.80 percentage points, increases normalized received power by 0.32 percentage points, and reduces outage probability by 2.06 percentage points without retraining the predictor.

title: Learning Lean Feedback for Efficient Proof-Candidate Evaluation on GPUs
abstract: Training language models for formal theorem proving requires large numbers of verifier calls. Slow checks and timeouts often leave GPUs waiting and withhold rewards from potentially correct proofs. We train neural evaluators to predict Lean 4 verdicts and compiler feedback on GPUs using 4.84M labelled programs. We compare two validity classifiers with a feedback model that annotates proof attempts with predicted goal states and error messages. A two-stage evaluator that screens candidates with a classifier and scores its positive predictions with the feedback model reaches 87.8% accuracy in predicting whether Lean accepts a candidate proof, evaluated on a 68,932-program benchmark collected from public provers. The combined evaluator processes 3.5 candidates per second on one H100, 4.2x the throughput of our 64-worker Lean baseline with environment reuse. Finally, we combine our evaluator with Lean verdicts to obtain a hybrid reward system that shortens GRPO training steps by approximately 31%. After one GRPO epoch with hybrid rewards, the prover achieves nearly the same miniF2F pass@1 as with Lean-only rewards (62.2% versus 62.4%) and a pass@32 of 72.4% versus 71.3%.

title: Anvil: Scaling Embodied Spatial Intelligence through Knowledge Recirculation
abstract: Embodied spatial intelligence requires more than visual recognition: models must localize entities, reason about their relations, and express this knowledge in action-relevant forms. Yet joint training can conflate the knowledge needed at different stages because supervision is fragmented across incompatible geometric and semantic outputs. We introduce Anvil, a unified framework for data generation, training, and benchmarking for embodied spatial intelligence. (1) Anvil-Gen is a heterogeneous data flywheel that combines form-specific generation, cross-stage consistency verification, and failure-driven recollection across 11 Ground--Relation--Act forms. (2) Anvil-Ben provides scene-aligned supervision for learning diverse embodied spatial capabilities and scene-linked assessments that distinguish stage competence from error propagation. (3) Anvil-MOPD is a 9B student that consolidates heterogeneous spatial knowledge through distillation from specialist teachers. Semantic-first-fault routing targets teacher supervision to the student's earliest decisive failure, while stage normalization controls the loss scale across native outputs of different lengths. We construct 5.8M source-grounded records spanning 160K images, reserving 580K spatial records for held-out evaluation and using the remaining 5.22M records for training. On average across seven public benchmarks, Anvil-MOPD outperforms Qwen3.5-9B and RynnBrain-8B by 9.29 and 11.03 percentage points, respectively, while reaching 80.67% on VABench-Point. Controlled studies support targeted coverage, selective transfer, and feedback-guided repair as complementary framework components.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Optimization for Emergency-Priority Traffic Signal Control
abstract: Emergency-priority traffic signal control requires reducing emergency-vehicle delay while limiting disruption to ordinary traffic. This work investigates a finite-horizon QUBO formulation and compares Exact QUBO optimization, QAOA, CVaR-QAOA, a quantum machine-learning policy, fixed-time control, and max-pressure control in a three-intersection corridor. The study evaluates three traffic-demand regimes, examines the effect of the emergency-priority weight, and compares quantum solutions with the exact QUBO optimum. The optimization-based controllers achieved reliable emergency progression across all tested demand regimes, while max-pressure produced lower ordinary-traffic delay. Increasing emergency priority reduced emergency travel time but increased congestion, with diminishing improvements at larger weights. CVaR-QAOA reproduced the exact QUBO solution more accurately than standard QAOA, although the resulting differences in closed-loop traffic performance were comparatively small.

title: Cohomogeneity one Hermann actions and backward mean curvature flows
abstract: Principal orbits of cohomogeneity one Hermann actions form a natural class of equifocal hypersurfaces in symmetric spaces of compact type. Based on Kollross's classification of cohomogeneity one actions on irreducible symmetric spaces of compact type, we obtain the time evolution of the squared norm of the shape operator and the mean curvature along the long-time solution of the backward mean curvature flows starting from their principal orbits. These results explicitly describe the authors' previous generalization of the results of Liu-Terng on backward mean curvature flows of isoparametric hypersurfaces to this class of equifocal hypersurfaces.

title: Scalar curvature, volume, and Weil-Petersson translation length
abstract: We construct metrics on pseudoAnosov mapping tori that make every fiber an intrinsically hyperbolic stable minimal surface, and which have scalar curvature identically -6. Using this, we give a new proof (with improved constant) of an inequality bounding the hyperbolic volume of a pseudoAnosov mapping torus by the Weil-Petersson translation length (and consequently, the entropy) of its monodromy.

title: Low-Scale See-Saw Mechanism and the Majorana Nature of Heavy Neutrinos
abstract: We investigate the possibility to determine the Majorana nature of the heavy Majorana neutrinos present in the low-scale type I seesaw mechanism of neutrino mass generation in experiments at $e^+ \text{-} e^-$ and $μ^+ \text{-} μ^-$ colliders. This is done on the examples of two specific symmetry-protected seesaw scenarios with two right-handed (RH) singlet neutrinos and one seesaw realization with three RH neutrinos. We use the forward-backward symmetry in the angular distribution of the heavy neutral leptons produced in the $e^+ \text{-} e^-$ and $μ^+ \text{-} μ^-$ collisions as an indicator of their Majorana nature. Our results indicate that the experiments at FCCee during its first phase of operation have a remarkable potential not only to discover the heavy neutral leptons associated with the type I seesaw mechanism if they have masses smaller than the $Z^0$-boson mass, but also to probe and provide evidence for their Majorana nature.

title: MetaShare: Failure-Aware Collective Self-Improvement for Open-Ended Agents
abstract: Humans often learn fastest not by repeating success, but by remembering which failures not to repeat. Open-ended self-improving agents can share experience across lineages, as in GEA, or edit their own improvement mechanisms, as in DGM-Hyperagents, yet failed improvement attempts are rarely retained as reusable cross-branch knowledge, and search can collapse onto redundant strategies. We introduce MetaShare, a failure-aware framework that records successful and unsuccessful agent modifications together with signed performance deltas. Before each generation, MetaShare retrieves diverse high-performing strategies alongside high-confidence failures from other lineages, letting agents reuse effective mechanisms while avoiding known dead ends. A task-blind auditor periodically injects absent or underrepresented mechanism categories, while embedding-based de-ranking limits redundancy during retrieval. Multiple meta-agents propose modifications in parallel at heterogeneous temperatures behind a deterministic selector that gates applicability, scope, compilability, and size. Experiments across paper review, coding, math grading, robotics reward design, and financial audit-risk assessment show that MetaShare's median matches or exceeds DGM-Hyperagents' final performance and reaches its own best-performing agent in 1.7--2.9$\times$ fewer evolution iterations.

title: Statistical Ambiguity-Function-Aware Joint Beamforming and Subcarrier Allocation for MIMO-OFDM ISAC under Random Symbols
abstract: Ambiguity function (AF) characterizes the delay--Doppler sidelobe structure that governs target resolution and masking in radar sensing. In ISAC, however, random communication symbols make the AF data-dependent, complicating its characterization and incorporation into transmit design. This raises a fundamental question: which AF characteristic can be effectively controlled through beamforming in a practical multiuser multitarget (MUMT) MIMO--OFDM system? To answer this, we statistically characterize the discrete-periodic AF (DP-AF) and derive an exact closed-form expected sidelobe level (ESL). We observe that nonzero-Doppler ESL cuts are delay-flat and the full two-dimensional integrated sidelobe level ratio (ISLR) is invariant to beamforming, whereas the zero-Doppler peak-to-sidelobe ratio (PSLR) remains controllable. We accordingly formulate an AF-aware joint beamforming and subcarrier-allocation problem with target-wise PSLR and illumination constraints. Since the direct PSLR constraint is intractable, we characterize its global optimum and prove that, for symbol kurtosis greater than one, the PSLR is maximized if and only if each target-wise directional-power profile is flat across subcarriers. We then introduce the coefficient of variation (CV) to measure deviation from this flatness and derive tight CV-dependent PSLR bounds. The lower bound yields a convex sufficient constraint for a desired PSLR, enabling an efficient reformulation. Simulations show $9.4$--$11.0$ dB worst-case PSLR gains over communication-only beamforming at the flat-spectrum point with a $2.4$--$5.9\%$ sum-rate loss. The CV-relaxed formulation achieves $99.7\%$ of the average sum-rate of the original PSLR-constrained problem, while reducing runtime by factors of $10.35$--$12.15$ under the considered scenarios.

title: Tauberian rates and the Baire property of ideals
abstract: We study Tauberian conditions on the successive differences of real sequences which ensure that: (i) ordinary convergence coincides with ideal convergence; or (ii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal cluster point; or (iii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal limit point. First, we prove that an ideal $\mathcal{I}$ has the Baire property if and only if there exists a positive sequence $(r_n)$ tending to zero, with $\sum_n r_n=\infty$, such that $$ |x_{n+1}-x_n|=O(r_n) $$ is a Tauberian condition for any of the three previous statements. Second, for analytic $P$-ideals, we characterize the validity of the Tauberian rate $O(1/n)$ in terms of properties of lower semicontinuous submeasures which represent it. Lastly, in the case of statistical limit points, we prove that $o(1/n)$ is a Tauberian condition for the statement (iii), whereas $O(1/n)$ need not suffice: in this sense, $o(1/n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for (iii). On the other hand, for statistical cluster points in (ii), $O(1/n)$ is an optimal one among nonincreasing rates. For every positive null sequence $(r_n)$ with divergent sum, we also construct a summable ideal $\mathcal{I}$ for which $o(r_n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for both statements (ii) and (iii).

title: GPU Parallel Pareto Local Search for Multi-objective QUBO
abstract: We revisit Pareto Local Search (PLS) for multi-objective quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems. Multi-objective QUBO formulations have gained increasing attention as a universal modeling method and natural input for quantum optimization. While exact methods exist, their unconstrained binary structure makes them well-suited for heuristics such as PLS. At the same time, GPUs offer a powerful classical alternative to quantum-inspired optimization. We develop an efficient GPU-based parallel implementation of PLS for multi-objective QUBO problems. Our approach combines coarse-grained and fine-grained parallelization. On the coarse-grained level, an initial set of supported solutions is generated using weighted-sum optimization, from which multiple PLS processes are started in parallel. At the fine-grained level, neighborhood exploration is parallelized on the GPU by simultaneously evaluating binary-flip candidate solutions across all objectives. Non-dominated solutions are maintained using an ND-Tree data structure to support efficient Pareto updates. The implementation combines several known PLS techniques within a unified CPU/GPU hybrid architecture. We describe the algorithmic components, the GPU-specific design decisions, and report results from a computational study evaluating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: From Scaling Relations to Physical Laws: Constraining the Physics of Star Formation Across Local Galaxies
abstract: The conversion of cold dense gas, traced by molecular line emission, into stars remains one of the fundamental unsolved problems in galaxy evolution. Observations over the past decades have established empirical relations between gas and star formation, yet their physical origin remains uncertain. Gravity, turbulence, and stellar feedback as main drivers provide fundamentally different pictures of how star formation is regulated, while reproducing remarkably similar galaxy-scale scaling relations. To disentangle the individual importance of each process, not only its mass and distribution, but also its temperature, density, excitation, and chemistry must be probed. However, current or planned (sub)millimetre facilities cannot combine statistical breadth, cloud-scale resolution, and multi-line diagnostics across large galaxy samples. A new, flagship interferometer with increased line sensitivity and bandwidth enables obtaining multi-transition, multi-isotopologue observations of molecular gas at GMC-resolved scales across nearby galaxies, enabling millions of independent measurements of its physical state across a wide range of extragalactic environments. This will transform molecular gas from an empirical tracer into a quantitative probe of the physical processes governing the relation between the dense gas and star formation. With the 2040s landscape of optical and radio facilities, ALMA2040 will facilitate a predictive theory of the conversion of gas into stars.

title: Graph Dirichlet Energy for Fitting-Free Bivariate Causal Inference
abstract: We propose the Graph Dirichlet Energy Causal Inference (GDECI) criterion for distinguishing cause from effect in bivariate settings. For a candidate direction $X\to Y$, we construct a kernel similarity graph from $X$ and treat $Y$ as a graph signal. The score is the Dirichlet energy of this signal, induced by the unnormalized graph Laplacian. The reverse score swaps the variables, and the lower-energy direction is inferred as causal. The method requires neither regression fitting nor independence testing. After the empirical probability integral transform, its decisions are invariant under strictly monotone transformations of either variable, and the graph operations reduce to convolutions, allowing exact evaluation in $O(n\log n)$ time and $O(n)$ memory. At the population level, GDECI compares degree-weighted Bayes squared prediction errors plus a non-negative smoothness term of the regression function. As the bandwidth tends to zero, the weights become uniform and the smoothness term vanishes, reducing the criterion to a RECI-type comparison of expected conditional variances in copula space. Empirically, we compare GDECI with QCCD, GRCI, CAM, IGCI (two variants), RESIT, LOCI, QPE-k, and RECI (two variants), in accuracy on 1899 cause--effect pairs and in inference speed. GDECI ranked fifth of eleven methods in macro-averaged accuracy on 12 synthetic suites ($0.776$). On the real-world Tuebingen pairs, it ranked third in unweighted accuracy ($0.684$) and fifth in weighted accuracy ($0.678$). It was also the fastest of the compared methods up to $n\approx10^{4}$. The accompanying code repository: https://github.com/povidanius/gdeci.

title: GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models
abstract: Context compression in long-running applications of large language models (LLMs) must preserve goal-relevant information, often before specific downstream questions are known. We introduce GACC-Bench, a benchmark for Goal-Adaptive Context Compression that evaluates how reliably LLMs adapt information retention to specified high-level goals. For each source context, we derive one or more high-level goals by grouping source-grounded questions according to shared downstream objectives. The benchmark contains 500 goals and 2,571 questions over 281 document and agent-trace contexts from seven collections spanning diverse domains, with all instances reviewed by human experts. The compressor receives a source context, a goal, and a context-length budget, with the associated evaluation questions withheld. A fixed reader answers these questions individually using the same compressed context. Our evaluation of ten LLM compressors reveals substantial gaps to full-context performance even for the best-performing model, particularly in supporting correct answers to every question associated with a goal. Compared with goal-agnostic compression, target-goal conditioning consistently improves accuracy, whereas mismatched-goal conditioning reduces it. GACC-Bench is available at https://github.com/weiting24/GACC-Bench.

title: A family of algebras that connects positroids, the Theta conjecture, the Delta conjecture, and Eulerian quasisymmetric functions
abstract: We define a family of algebras $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,a,b}$ whose Hilbert series, when $n\le a+b\le n+2$, $a>0$, and $0<b<n$, enumerate certain positroid cells by codimension. Equivalently, these series enumerate certain affine permutations by length. We determine the graded $\mathfrak{S}_n$-module structure of these algebras by using exact sequences to derive an invertible recursion for their graded Frobenius characteristics when $a+b\ge n$ and then passing to the limit $a\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the graded Frobenius characteristic $\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b-1}]/I_{a+b-1,a,b};q)=\operatorname{rev}_q(ω((Θ_{e_{a-1}}Θ_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\operatorname{rev}_q$ reverses the $q$-coefficients and the specialization $(Θ_{e_{a-1}}Θ_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}$ appears in the Theta conjecture. For $a,b\ge1$, we also show that $e_a^\perp\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b}]/I_{a+b,a,b};q)=q^{\binom{a}{2}}\operatorname{rev}_q(ω((Δ_{e_{a-1}}^\prime e_b)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $Δ_{e_{k-1}}^\prime e_n$ occurs in the Delta conjecture. In the three cases $a+b-n=0,1,2$, the ungraded Frobenius characteristics agree with three families of Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, respectively. We also construct an open subvariety of $(\mathbb{P}^{k-1})^n$ whose rational Chow ring is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k}$. This variety admits a stratification induced by certain positroids. Its strata need not be affine, and their codimension generating function equals $\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k};q)$.

title: SurgStreamer: proactive, request-driven monitoring of surgical video streams with structured state and a reusable reasoning layer
abstract: Surgical teams could benefit from assistants that watch the video for requested events, such as "tell me when the clip applier appears during Calot triangle dissection", and answer questions about what has already happened. We formalise this task as request-driven event detection with exact semantics and causal alert decisions, and present SurgStreamer. It separates procedure-specific perception, which maps the 1-FPS stream to a structured state over tools, actions and phases, from procedure-agnostic reasoning, which evaluates a formal monitoring condition over this state and an event memory, either with exact rules or with a small controller that addresses entities through pointers rather than names. We evaluate this monitoring core with gold conditions. On a pre-registered, sealed test set of 12 laparoscopic cholecystectomies, SurgStreamer reached a macro event-F1 of 0.598 over full procedures. On identical 75-s windows with only the window available to every method, it scored 0.677. The tested configurations of the streaming vision-language model OneStreamer-4B, including ones fine-tuned on SurgStreamer's state or on video with an adapted vision encoder, scored at most 0.540 (Holm-adjusted p <= 0.012). At three external centres, re-training only perception raised performance on held-out procedures from 0.239 to 0.470. On a new procedure, pituitary surgery, controller weights trained on cholecystectomy matched an in-domain controller on oracle state (0.947 vs 0.938). On predicted state they missed the pre-registered non-inferiority margin (-0.024 [-0.040, -0.008]) unless the alert thresholds were re-calibrated. The results support separating perception from reasoning and point to perception under distribution shift as the main limitation.

title: Self-Calibrated Subspace Robust PCA for Parameter-Free Removal of Mixed Noise and Line Stripes in Hyperspectral Images
abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) are often corrupted by Gaussian noise, impulses and stripes whose intensities vary across bands. The representative coefficient correlated total variation (RCCTV) model restores HSIs efficiently, but it lacks Gaussian and stripe terms, and its noise-aware extensions require the noise level and a stripe budget to be specified in advance. This article proposes a self-calibrated RCCTV (SC-RCCTV) model, in which the noise parameters are estimated adaptively during the iterations. A band-wise dense term and line-constant column and row stripe terms are introduced into RCCTV. The noise level of each band is initialized by a stripe-invariant median absolute deviation estimator and refined online from the residual, which turns the separation of sparse and dense noise into a band-adaptive Huber loss, and the stripe thresholds follow from a significance test whose false-alarm rate can be predicted analytically. No parameter is tuned for a specific image, and every subproblem of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) solver is solved in closed form. Under line stripes, SC-RCCTV outperforms the parameter-free FastHyMix by 8.17 dB on native-size cubes, and, without any noise information, it exceeds S3TTV, which is given the true noise parameters, by 1.52 dB while running more than 1,900 times faster. On average, it stays within 0.01 dB of the same model given the true noise levels, and its online calibration improves on a two-stage estimate-then-denoise scheme. Experiments on real Indian Pines and Urban data further delineate its scope for stripes that do not span entire lines.

title: Lossy Lorentz boosts at ultra-relativistic energies: Numerical study and source survey of high-energy physics software
abstract: Most high-energy-physics software packages implement Lorentz boosts for themselves.
